title: B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter – Healthcare Services
description:
# B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter – Healthcare Services



**Remote | Part-Time | 20–25 Hours/Week**



We are a mobile phlebotomy company serving healthcare providers, senior communities, home health organizations, medical practices, laboratories, and other healthcare organizations throughout Michigan.



We are looking for an **experienced B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter** to introduce our services to prospective business clients and help us develop new partnerships.



This is **NOT a general virtual assistant position.**



Your primary responsibility will be **outbound calling and business development.** You should be comfortable making a high volume of calls every day and speaking confidently with office managers, administrators, physicians' offices, laboratory representatives, home health agencies, senior living facilities, and other healthcare organizations.



### What You'll Do



* Make a high volume of outbound B2B cold calls

* Contact hundreds of prospective companies and healthcare organizations

* Introduce US Mobile Lab and clearly explain our services

* Identify the appropriate decision-maker within each organization

* Navigate receptionists and gatekeepers professionally

* Ask questions to determine whether the organization could benefit from our services

* Generate qualified leads and schedule follow-up conversations

* Follow up with interested prospects by phone and

* Maintain accurate notes and update lead status

* Build and organize prospect lists when necessary

* Learn our services well enough to have a natural conversation instead of simply reading a script



### Who We're Looking For



**Excellent spoken English is REQUIRED.**



You must be able to communicate clearly, naturally, and professionally with U.S.-based businesses.



The ideal candidate has:



* Highly fluent or near-native spoken English

* Strong, easy-to-understand pronunciation

* Previous **cold-calling, telesales, appointment-setting, or B2B sales experience**

* Confidence speaking with business owners, managers, and healthcare professionals

* The ability to sound conversational rather than scripted

* Experience handling objections and getting past gatekeepers

* Strong phone presence and personality

* Persistence without being overly aggressive

* Ability to make a large number of calls consistently

* Good organizational and follow-up skills

* Reliable internet and a quiet, professional calling environment



Healthcare sales experience is a plus, but **strong cold-calling ability is more important.**



### What Success Looks Like



We are not looking for someone who simply completes a certain number of calls.



We want someone who can turn cold prospects into conversations.



You should be comfortable hearing "no," continuing to the next prospect, following up consistently, and figuring out how to reach the right decision-maker.



Our goal is to introduce US Mobile Lab to **hundreds of potential partner organizations** and develop long-term business relationships.



### Schedule



Approximately **20–25 hours per week**, primarily during U.S. Eastern Time business hours.



### Compensation



Starting compensation will depend on experience and demonstrated cold-calling ability.



There may also be opportunities for **performance-based bonuses for qualified appointments or new accounts generated.**



### IMPORTANT – How to Apply



Please include:



1. Your previous cold-calling or appointment-setting experience.

2. Approximately how many outbound calls you are comfortable making per day.

3. What types of businesses or industries you have called previously.

4. A **30–60 second voice recording** introducing yourself and explaining why you would be a good fit for this position.

title: Hourly DevOps/Linux: Walkthrough to Deploy Docker WebRTC Apps on VPS
description:

I want to perform the terminal steps myself on my screen while you explain what we are doing, answer my questions, and help troubleshoot any issues that pop up in real time.



Scope of Work (What We Will Set Up Together):



1. DNS & Subdomains: Point two subdomains (e.g., 
 and 
) to my Hostinger VPS IP address.



2. Docker App Deployment:

- Deploy msitarzewski/openstudio (OpenStudio podcast studio) in its Docker container.

- Deploy miroslavpejic85/mirotalksfu (MiroTalk SFU video call room) in its Docker container.

Engagement Details:

title: Ecommerce Customer Service Representative (Shopify)
description:
PLEASE READ THIS ENTIRE JOB POST BEFORE APPLYING



ABOUT THE ROLE



We are a fast-growing 7-figure DTC eCommerce brand looking for an experienced and exceptional Customer Service Representative to join our team.



This isn't just another customer service job.



We're looking for someone who is driven, adaptable, proactive, and genuinely excited to grow with a company long-term.



We value attitude, work ethic, and the willingness to improve. However, applicants must already have a strong foundation in e-commerce customer service and hands-on experience with the tools required for this role.



IMPORTANT: STRICT EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS



Please read the following requirements carefully before applying.



These are NON-NEGOTIABLE requirements.



1. HANDS-ON SHOPIFY EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED



Applicants must have previous hands-on experience using Shopify in an e-commerce customer service role.



You should be comfortable navigating Shopify, reviewing orders, checking customer and order details, and handling basic e-commerce-related tasks.



If you have never used Shopify before, please DO NOT APPLY.



2. PREVIOUS E-COMMERCE CUSTOMER SERVICE EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED



You must have previous experience working in e-commerce customer service.



We are no longer accepting applicants without prior e-commerce customer service experience.



This role requires individuals who already understand the fundamentals of handling customer inquiries, order concerns, refunds, replacements, shipping issues, and other common e-commerce support scenarios.



If you have no previous e-commerce customer service experience, please DO NOT APPLY.



3. EXPERIENCE WITH AT LEAST ONE CUSTOMER SERVICE PLATFORM IS REQUIRED



You must have hands-on experience using at least ONE of the following customer service or helpdesk platforms:



- Richpanel

- CommsLayer

- Front

- Zendesk

- Gorgias



You should have actual experience using the platform to handle customer inquiries or manage customer support tickets.



Experience with other comparable helpdesk or customer service platforms may also be considered, provided you have genuinely used the platform in a customer support role.



If you have no experience using ANY of the platforms listed above, or any comparable customer service helpdesk platform, please DO NOT APPLY.



AUTOMATIC DISQUALIFICATION



To respect everyone's time, please do not apply if you do not meet the minimum experience requirements outlined above.



Applicants who do not have:



- Hands-on Shopify experience

- Previous e-commerce customer service experience

- Experience using at least one of the required customer service platforms or a comparable helpdesk system



will be automatically declined.



We are looking for experienced candidates who can adapt to our workflows, follow our SOPs, and contribute to the team without requiring training on the fundamentals of e-commerce customer service.



Please be honest about your experience. We value transparency and would rather work with someone who accurately represents their skills and background.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



We're looking for someone who:



- Has excellent written English with strong grammar, spelling, and communication skills.

- Has proven experience working in e-commerce customer service.

- Is confident navigating Shopify and customer service platforms.

- Learns quickly and enjoys mastering new systems and processes.

- Is proactive and takes initiative instead of waiting to be told what to do.

- Can work independently with minimal supervision.

- Is resourceful and knows how to find answers before asking for help.

- Accepts feedback professionally and applies it immediately.

- Is adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where processes continue to improve.

- Is willing to unlearn habits from previous companies and fully adopt our workflows, SOPs, and standards.

- Takes pride in producing high-quality work instead of simply completing a shift.

- Is looking for a long-term opportunity rather than just another VA job.

- Can commit to being fully focused and productive during scheduled working hours.



PREFERRED EXPERIENCE



The following experience is a plus and will be considered an advantage:



- Experience handling subscription-based e-commerce businesses.

- Experience navigating or using Loop Subscriptions.

- Experience with Checkout Champ.

- Experience with other subscription management platforms.

- Familiarity with subscription cancellations, billing inquiries, subscription modifications, and recurring order management.

- Experience working with multiple e-commerce tools and systems.



These are preferred qualifications, not strict requirements. However, candidates with relevant subscription management experience may be better prepared for some of the responsibilities of this role.



RESPONSIBILITIES



You'll be responsible for:



- Responding to customer
s professionally and empathetically.

- Resolving customer concerns efficiently and accurately.

- Handling order updates, shipping inquiries, refunds, replacements, and product questions.

- Assisting customers with subscription-related concerns, including cancellations, billing questions, and subscription changes.

- Navigating Shopify and relevant customer service systems to investigate and resolve customer issues.

- Following company SOPs while adapting to new processes as the business grows.

- Documenting and managing customer interactions accurately.

- Escalating complex issues when necessary.

- Delivering a consistently excellent customer experience.

- Maintaining high standards of quality, accuracy, and professionalism.



COMPENSATION & GROWTH



- Starting rate: $4 USD/hour.

- New hires will begin on a part-time trial period.

- High-performing team members who consistently demonstrate reliability, initiative, and strong performance will have the opportunity to transition into a full-time position (40–48 hours/week).

- Performance bonuses may be available based on company policies and individual performance. (KPIs)

- Opportunities for additional responsibilities and career growth as the company continues to expand.



We're looking for someone who wants to build a long-term career with the company.



Preference will be given to applicants who can make our team their primary work commitment. Applicants with other part-time jobs or client commitments may still be considered, provided they fully disclose these commitments during the application process.



If you currently work with another employer or client, please include the following information in your application:

-Your preferred working schedule with us.

-The days and hours you currently work for your other employer or client.

-Your availability outside of those working hours.



This information will help us assess your availability and determine potential scheduling arrangements if you progress through the interview process.



Please be honest and transparent about your current work commitments. Full disclosure is important to us when evaluating candidates for long-term opportunities with our team.



OUR HIRING PROCESS



We invest heavily in building a strong team, so our hiring process is designed to identify candidates who are willing to learn, follow instructions, and grow with the company.



1. Submit your application.

2. Selected applicants will receive a short application form.

3. Top candidates will be invited for an interview.

4. Successful interviewees will receive access to our learning materials for a self-paced learning period (approximately one week).

5. Before the end of that week, you'll complete a timed mock customer support assessment based on the materials provided.

6. Candidates who successfully pass the assessment will proceed to the paid training stage, with the opportunity to become a long-term member of our team.



Please note:



The evaluation stage is designed to assess your ability to learn, follow SOPs, and apply new knowledge to real-world customer support scenarios.



Only candidates who successfully pass the evaluation stage will move on to paid training.



REQUIREMENTS



- At least 18 years old.

- Fluent in written English.

- Strong grammar, spelling, and communication skills.

- Previous hands-on Shopify experience.

- Previous e-commerce customer service experience.

- Hands-on experience using at least one of the required customer service platforms listed in this post, or a comparable helpdesk system.

- Reliable computer and internet connection.

- Able to work independently with minimal supervision.

- Strong attention to detail.

- Willingness to learn and continuously improve.

- Ability to follow company SOPs and adapt to changing workflows.

- Strong problem-solving skills.



HOW TO APPLY



To confirm that you've read this entire job post, please follow all the instructions below.



1. Include the word PURPLE at the beginning of your application title.



2. Answer the following questions:



- How many years of e-commerce customer service experience do you have?

- How long have you been using Shopify? Briefly describe the tasks you regularly handled in Shopify.

- Which customer service or helpdesk platforms have you used? Please list all the platforms you have hands-on experience with and describe how you used them.

- Have you worked with subscription-based e-commerce businesses? If yes, which subscription platforms have you used?

- What motivates you to do great work?

- Why do you want to work with our company?

- How do you usually handle constructive feedback?

- If you don't know the answer to a customer's question, what would you do?



3. BONUS EXERCISE



A customer sends the following
:



"I've already
ed twice and nobody has helped me. This is honestly very frustrating."



Write the response you would send to this customer.



4. EXPERIENCE VERIFICATION



Please include the following information in your application:



- Your previous e-commerce customer service experience.

- The Shopify stores or types of e-commerce businesses you have worked with.

- The customer service platforms you have used.

- The subscription management tools you have experience with, if any.



Please do not share confidential information from previous employers.



We carefully review every application.



Thoughtful answers, genuine hands-on experience, and attention to detail matter much more than generic responses or years of experience alone.



If you meet all the strict requirements and are confident in your ability to deliver high-quality customer service, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Zoning & Land Development Analyst – GIS / Geodetic / Civil Engineering
description:
We are a U.S.-based real estate development company looking for a Zoning & Land Development Analyst to help us evaluate land for new townhome developments.



Your primary job will be to answer one important question:



How many townhomes can we realistically build on this property?



We have a large master list of potential development properties. You will research each property, analyze its zoning and physical characteristics, and determine its preliminary development potential.



Once we know the estimated number of buildable units, our team can underwrite the property and determine what we can afford to pay for the land.



What You'll Do

Research zoning and permitted uses for each property

Determine allowable residential density and potential number of townhome units

Research setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, parking requirements, minimum lot sizes, and other development standards

Review GIS and parcel maps

Review property boundaries, dimensions, access, easements, rights-of-way, and other potential constraints

Identify flood zones, utilities, topography, and other issues that may affect development

Review city/county zoning codes, development standards, maps, and public records

Estimate a preliminary buildable unit count based on our standardized townhome design

Clearly document your research, assumptions, and conclusions

Flag properties that require additional professional or municipal confirmation

Work through a high volume of properties from our master mailing list

Ideal Background



We are especially interested in candidates with experience or education in:



Geodetic Engineering / Land Surveying

Civil Engineering

GIS / Mapping

Zoning or Land Use

Urban Planning

Land Development / Site Planning

Development Feasibility



Experience working with U.S. properties is a plus, but not required. We can teach you our process and the specific markets we work in.



Who We're Looking For



You should be analytical, highly detail-oriented, comfortable researching technical information, and good at reading maps, parcel information, surveys, and development standards.



You should also be able to work independently, stay organized, communicate clearly, and know when something needs additional review rather than making assumptions.



This is not a sales position. It is a focused research and analysis role for someone who enjoys land, maps, zoning, engineering, and solving development problems.



If you have worked as a Geodetic Engineer, Land Surveyor, GIS Analyst, Zoning Technician, Civil Engineer, or similar technical role, we would especially like to hear from you.



To Apply



Please send us a short voice recording introducing yourself and briefly explaining your relevant experience.

title: Outbound Appointment Setter, US Retirement
description:
We call people in the United States who have asked for information about retirement income. You find out what they are trying to work out, check whether they fit, and then connect them live to a licensed insurance agent. You introduce the two of them and drop off the call.



You are not selling anything. You are not licensed and you will not be. If a caller asks you what a product pays or whether they should buy it, the answer is always that the agent will cover it.



- **$5.00 USD per hour**, paid for every hour you work

- **$3 for every transfer the client accepts.** $4 each once you pass 10 accepted in a week, $5 each once you pass 20. This resets every week

- **$15 bonus** in any week where 80% or more of your transfers are accepted and at least 10 were accepted

- Paid every two weeks, in USD



A typical week at 40 hours and 15 accepted transfers works out around $265.



One thing to be clear about, because it surprises people. The per-transfer pay is on transfers the **client accepts**. If you connect somebody who turns out to be in the wrong state, or well under the asset range, or who did not understand what the call was, the client rejects it and it does not pay. If it had already been paid, it comes off a later period. Your hourly base is never affected by any of this.



We would rather have three transfers a day that the client accepts than ten that fall apart. Three a day is what puts you into the higher rate tier, and if your acceptance rate holds at 80% or better it also earns the weekly bonus. The pay is built around quality, not volume.



**What you need**



- Clear spoken English. Our callers are 55 and older and they need to understand you the first time

- A wired USB headset with a microphone

- A computer that can run a dialer and two browser tabs without struggling

- Reliable internet, **25 Mbps down and 10 up minimum**, wired preferred, and a plan for when the power goes

- A quiet place to work with no background noise

- Able to work 9:00pm to 6:00am Manila, Monday to Saturday



**What we are looking for**



Someone who can follow a script and still sound like a person. Someone who does not push. The most expensive mistake in this job is talking somebody onto the line who did not want to be there, so if your instinct is to keep going until you get a yes, we are not a fit.



**What the process is**



1. You fill in one form. 
 

It takes about ten minutes and it ends with a 60-second voice recording. 

2. We score it and reply either way.

3. A 20-minute interview on video. Ten minutes of it is a role-play, where you read our opening and handle two objections. We send you the script in advance.

4. An offer.



We reply to everyone who submits a voice sample.

Submit your application here: 

To show you read this: start your 60-second voice recording with the word: "Pineapple"

title: Outbound Sales Rep / Appointment Setter — US Retirement Calls — Night Shift (PH, WFH)
description:
What the job actually is



This is an outbound sales role. You are on the phone all shift.



We call people in the United States who filled in a form about retirement income and life insurance. Most of them will not remember filling it in. Your job is to open the call, explain who we are and why we are calling, get them interested enough to keep talking, ask the questions that tell you whether they fit what our client is looking for, and then hand the good ones live to a licensed agent.



You sell the conversation. You never sell the product.



That one line is the whole job. You have to create enough interest that a stranger agrees to speak with an agent. What you never do is discuss the product itself: no recommending it, no quoting a rate or a return, no telling anybody whether they should buy. You are not licensed and you will not be. Every product question gets the same answer, warmly: "That's exactly what the licensed agent will walk you through on the call."



If you have sold anything over the phone before, the skill transfers. If you have only ever read scripts and logged outcomes, this will be harder than you expect.



We are Apex Digital Media, a Florida company. On calls you use our brand name, Summers Ahead.



The hours



9:00am to 6:00pm US Eastern Time, Monday to Saturday.



In Manila that is 9:00pm to 6:00am. From early November to mid March it shifts to 10:00pm to 7:00am, when the US changes its clocks.



This is a permanent night shift. Our consumers are in the United States and you can only legally call them during their day. There is no night differential and no rotation onto days later. If a permanent night schedule does not work for your life, this is not the job.



The pay, in full

$5.00 USD per hour, for every hour you work

$3 for every transfer the client accepts. $4 each once you pass 10 accepted in a week, $5 each once you pass 20. Resets every week

$15 bonus in any week where at least 10 transfers are accepted and 80% or more of your transfers are accepted

Paid every two weeks in USD. The period closes Saturday 11:59 PM ET and you are paid the following Friday

Your first payment lands 6 to 19 days after your first shift, depending which day of the cycle you start on



A typical week at 40 hours and 15 accepted transfers is around $265.



Read this part twice. Transfer pay is on transfers the client accepts, not transfers you make. Connect somebody in the wrong state, well outside the income range, or who did not really understand what the call was, and the client rejects it. A rejected transfer pays nothing. If it was already paid, it comes off your next period. That is a clawback and it will happen to you at some point.



Your hourly base is never touched by any of this. It is for your time, and your time was worked.



This is why pressure does not pay here. Three accepted transfers a day beats ten that fall apart, and three a day is what moves you into the higher rate tier.



The hard parts, so you can d
 now



You are starting most calls cold, from a standing start. "I never signed up for anything" is something you will hear many times a day. You need to be able to explain calmly what they filled in and re-earn the conversation. If somebody genuinely does not remember, or asks you to stop, you take them off the list and end the call. You do not argue them into it.



Most dials go nowhere. New hires work the oldest, hardest lists for their first two weeks. That is where you learn the script without burning good leads. It is normal for the first fortnight to feel like nothing is working.



Your pay moves with quality, in both directions. Up with accepted transfers, down when they are rejected.



We track time with Hubstaff, which records your hours and takes periodic screenshots and activity readings while you are on shift. You are being told this now, before you apply, rather than after you accept.



Your first two weeks are a trial. At the end of it you either join the team properly or we stop. You are told exactly what is measured on day one, with check-ins at day 3, day 7 and day 14. Nothing about it is a surprise.



If you have read this far and still want it, you are the person we want to interview.



What we are looking for



Someone who can take a stranger who did not expect the call and turn it into a real conversation. That takes warmth, quick thinking, and the willingness to keep going after the first brush-off.



It does not take pressure. There are two ways to fail this job and both are common. One is reading the script and accepting the first no. The other is talking somebody onto the line who did not want to be there, which gets the transfer rejected, costs you the pay, and costs us the client. The skill is the middle: persuasive about the call, never pushy about the person.



Outbound sales, telemarketing or collections experience all help. Insurance experience is genuinely not needed. We teach that part.



What you need

Clear spoken English. Our consumers are 55 and older and they need to understand you the first time

A wired USB headset with a microphone

A computer that can run a dialer and two browser tabs without struggling

Internet at 25 Mbps down and 10 up minimum, wired preferred, and a plan for when the power goes

A quiet room with a door

Able to work 11:00am to 7:00pm ET, Monday to Saturday

The process

One form, about ten minutes, ending with a 60-second voice recording: [FORM LINK]

We score it and reply either way

A 20-minute video interview. Ten minutes of it is a role-play where you open a call and handle two objections. We send you the script in advance

An offer, then paid training from day one



We reply to everyone who submits a voice sample.



How to apply







To show you read this, start your recording with the word SUMMERS.

title: Video Editor for 2 of my YOUTUBE Channels
description:
I have 3 YouTube channels, and I need a new editor who can use DaVinci Resolve and has a good eye for editing videos. I use a cloud-based team editing approach, which means you will need to learn to edit from proxy files and have the storage space to do it. You will need to edit about 4-5 videos a month. I pay $130 per video, and I give a $100 bonus if all the videos are done on time by the end of the month.



REQUIREMENTS

1. YOU MUST BE ABLE TO USE DAVINCI RESOLVE and learn to edit from the cloud. (You can use the free version for the trial, but you need the full version after)

2. After the paid trial, you will need 1.3 TB of AVAILABLE STORAGE SPACE for all the proxies.

3. YOU MUST HAVE QUICK COMMUNICATION and DELIVER VIDEOS ON TIME.



APPLICATION:

Please respond by letting me know what you use to edit and how much storage space you will have to edit with on your device. You also MUST respond with a portfolio or examples of LONG-FORM videos that you have done. Even if they aren't professional, I can tell who has a good eye for editing. 



TEAM EDITING PROCESS

My projects are based on team editing, so I can leave notes on the project for you to fix, and I can even edit the video myself. So the process is probably different from what you're used to.



My process involves: 1- Downloading the proxies from my server to your device. 2- Chopping up the A-roll. 3- Adding B-roll. 4- Adding graphics, text, Titles, Transitions, and Music. 5- Changing the revisions that I send.



THE KIND OF VIDEOS & PROJECTS:

The current channels for this job listing are Baseline Dental and Brielle Buck, which are both on YouTube. Please watch some of the videos already posted on those channels. Once you understand my process and edit well, you can expect to make $650 to $750 per month at first, doing 4 to 5 videos a month. If you edit fast and on time, I will move you on to other projects, shorts, and possibly other channels. 



My other channel is called The Proposal. However, at first we'll work only with the Baseline Dental and Brielle Buck channels.



PAID TRIAL:

$130 if you complete this paid trial. The process will take a few days to learn and set up. But after a month or two it will get faster.



WHAT IS EXPECTED DURING THE TRIAL:

Once I
 you for the trial position, I expect you to start the process within 24 hours and start editing within a few days. I also expect the projects to be done well and on time. I expect all project rough drafts to be completed each month before the 21st. I expect you to have a good eye for video editing.



I have current editors who have worked with me for 6 years. I have been on YouTube for over 8 years. So this can be a reliable long-term job for you. I hope you will be my next editor!



Please apply and respond if you have used DaVinci and can deliver videos reliably and on time. Talk to you soon!

description:
Founder Content Writer / Ghostwriter - LinkedIn, X and Newsletter



We are looking for one dedicated writer to become the long-term writing partner to a UK-based founder/operator in e-commerce and social commerce.



This is not a generic social media manager role and it is not high-volume SEO writing. The job is to learn one founder's voice, extract strong ideas from conversations and source material, and turn them into sharp, useful content across LinkedIn, X and a weekly newsletter.



The current content operation already has an audience, source material and a working publishing rhythm. We now want one person who can build context over time, improve the quality and own the writing consistently. You will work directly with the founder and internal team. The role will not be passed between writers.



What you will own:

- A weekly 30-45 minute content interview with the founder

- 4-5 LinkedIn posts per week across different formats

- 1-3 longer article-style X posts or threads per week

- One newsletter per week

- Research, fact-checking and turning company/client insights into useful content without exposing confidential details

- A simple editorial calendar, revisions and a record of what performs

- Repurposing ideas across channels without copying the same post word-for-word



You may be a fit if:

- You have written in a founder, executive or subject-matter expert's voice before

- Your English is excellent and your writing sounds natural, specific and human

- You can interview someone, spot the strongest angle and challenge weak ideas

- You understand the differences between LinkedIn, X and

- You are comfortable writing about e-commerce, marketing, agencies, creator commerce or adjacent business topics

- You are reliable, responsive and want a long-term role with one team



This is not a fit if your experience is mainly generic blogs, AI-generated content, captions or scheduling. Tools can support research and editing, but the thinking, interviewing and final writing must be yours. You must personally write the work; no subcontracting.



To apply, send:

1. Three relevant samples, ideally content ghostwritten for a founder or executive. Explain what you personally wrote.

2. A short note on how you learn and maintain someone's voice.

3. One example of a time you turned an interview, call or rough notes into a strong piece of content.

4. Your location, working hours and availability to overlap with 9am-1pm UK time.

5. Your desired monthly rate within the range shown.



Shortlisted candidates will have a brief interview and a paid work sample using the same source material. Test work will not be published without separate agreement.



This starts with a 6-week paid contract and is intended to become a long-term, full-time role if the fit is strong.





Location: Philippines, remote. Full-time contractor. USD $1,000-$1,600 per month depending on experience and evidence of fit. A reliable daily overlap with 9am-1pm UK time is required; applicants should state the exact hours they can maintain.

title: Land Development Feasibility Analyst – Surveying / GIS / Zoning
description:
We are a U.S. real estate development company looking for a Land Development Feasibility Analyst to help us identify properties suitable for townhome development.



The main goal of this position is simple:



Analyze a parcel of land and determine approximately how many townhomes we can build on it.



We have a large database of potential development sites. You will work through these properties, research the applicable zoning and development requirements, review the physical characteristics of the land, and estimate the property's potential unit count.



Your analysis will then be used by our team to underwrite the property and determine the appropriate land purchase price.



Responsibilities

Research zoning classifications and permitted residential uses

Determine allowable density and potential townhome unit count

Research setbacks, parking requirements, lot coverage, height limits, minimum lot dimensions, and other development standards

Review GIS maps, parcel maps, assessor information, and public records

Analyze parcel dimensions, shape, road access, easements, and rights-of-way

Identify potential issues involving flood zones, utilities, drainage, topography, or other site constraints

Research city and county zoning ordinances

Evaluate whether a property appears suitable for our townhome development model

Document findings and assumptions clearly

Flag properties that require additional research or professional review

Background We're Looking For



Candidates with backgrounds in any of the following are strongly encouraged to apply:



Geodetic Engineering

Land Surveying

Civil Engineering

GIS / Geospatial Analysis

Zoning

Urban Planning

Land Development

Site Planning



You do not need extensive U.S. real estate experience. We are more interested in finding someone with a strong technical understanding of land who can learn our development process.



Ideal Candidate



You enjoy working with maps, land data, zoning regulations, and technical information.



You are analytical, detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable researching a problem until you find the answer.



Most importantly, you understand that determining development potential requires more than simply looking at acreage. Zoning, density, setbacks, access, easements, parcel configuration, utilities, and other constraints can all affect how many units can actually be built.



This is a long-term opportunity for the right person.



To Apply



Please send a short voice recording introducing yourself and briefly describing your relevant experience.

title: Senior Social Media Content Strategist & Video Editor
description:
# Senior Social Media Content Strategist & Video Editor



**Full-Time | Remote | Long-Term Position**

**Compensation: $1,000–$1,500 USD/month + Performance Bonuses**



## THIS IS NOT A BASIC SOCIAL MEDIA VA POSITION.



PB Agency is looking for an exceptional **Social Media Content Strategist & Video Editor** who understands what makes people STOP scrolling, WATCH content, SHARE it, and eventually BUY.



We are a fast-growing U.S.-based marketing agency working with entrepreneurs, educators, experts, and personal brands.



We do not need someone who simply waits for us to tell them what to post.



We need someone who can look at a brand and say:



**“Here are 10 content ideas we should create this week—and here's why I believe they'll work.”**



If you constantly study Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, creators, trends, hooks, editing styles, storytelling, and viral content, we want to hear from you.



## YOUR ROLE



You will help PB Agency and our clients develop and execute high-performing organic social media content.



You will be responsible for the entire content process:



**IDEA → STRATEGY → EDIT → POST → ANALYZE → IMPROVE**



### Your Responsibilities



* Develop new content ideas every week

* Research emerging social media trends

* Study competitors and successful creators

* Identify viral content formats we can adapt for our brands

* Create strong hooks and opening sequences

* Edit short-form videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts and

* Repurpose long-form videos, podcasts, Zoom calls and trainings into short-form content

* Edit long-form YouTube content when necessary

* Add captions, B-roll, graphics, zooms, pattern interrupts and other retention elements

* Create social graphics and carousels

* Write captions and post copy

* Schedule and publish content

* Maintain content calendars

* Organize raw and completed content

* Monitor content performance

* Review views, retention, engagement, shares, saves and other performance metrics

* Identify what's working and recommend what we should create next



Most importantly:



**You are expected to BRING IDEAS to the company—not just execute ours.**



## WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR



You should have at least **2–3 years of professional social media/content experience**.



You should understand:



* Instagram Reels

* TikTok

* YouTube Shorts

* YouTube long-form

*

* Personal-brand content

* Educational content

* Direct-response content

* Storytelling

* Hooks

* Viewer retention

* Pattern interrupts

* Content repurposing

* Social media algorithms

* Trend identification



You should be highly proficient with tools such as:



* Adobe Premiere Pro

* CapCut

* Final Cut Pro

* After Effects

* Canva

* Photoshop

* AI content tools



You don't need to know every program listed above.



**We care about your OUTPUT more than the software you use.**



## YOU MAY BE A GREAT FIT IF...



You watch a Reel and immediately think about why the first 3 seconds worked.



You notice editing styles before most people notice they're becoming trends.



You can take a 45-minute podcast and identify the 10 moments most likely to perform as short-form content.



You can study successful creators and reverse-engineer why their content works.



You understand that great editing isn't about adding random effects—it's about maintaining attention.



You are comfortable receiving feedback and making changes quickly.



You don't need someone constantly telling you what to do.



And you're obsessed with becoming exceptional at social media.



## THIS POSITION IS NOT FOR YOU IF...



You only know how to schedule posts.



You need someone to provide every content idea.



You consider yourself primarily a virtual assistant.



You have never professionally edited videos.



You don't actively consume and study social media.



You cannot explain why one piece of content performed better than another.



You are managing 10 freelance clients and looking for another one.



We're looking for someone who wants to become a **long-term member of PB Agency.**



## COMPENSATION



**Starting Compensation: $1,000–$1,500 USD/month**



Final compensation depends on experience, portfolio, editing ability, strategic thinking and demonstrated results.



There will also be opportunities for:



* Performance bonuses

* Compensation increases

* Increased responsibility

* Leadership opportunities



An exceptional person could eventually grow into a **Head of Content / Creative Director** position within PB Agency.



## HOW TO APPLY



Do NOT send us a generic application.



At the very top of your application write:



**“I WANT TO BUILD PB.”**



Then send us:



1. Your resume

2. Your portfolio

3. Your 5 BEST short-form videos

4. Your 2 BEST long-form videos, if available

5. Links to social media accounts you've helped manage or grow

6. Any screenshots showing results you've generated

7. Your current/most recent monthly compensation

8. Your expected monthly compensation



Then answer these questions:



**QUESTION #1**



Send us 3 creators or brands that you believe are producing some of the best social media content right now.



Explain WHY you chose each one.



**QUESTION #2**



If we gave you a 60-minute podcast episode, explain how you would turn it into 15+ pieces of social media content.



**QUESTION #3**



What do you believe separates a video that gets 5,000 views from one that gets 500,000+ views?



**QUESTION #4**



What social media trend or content format do you believe businesses are currently underutilizing?



Explain why.



## FINAL STEP



Candidates who make it through the initial application will receive a **PAID content test.**



We will provide raw footage.



You will be asked to:



* Identify the strongest content angle

* Write 3 potential hooks

* Edit one short-form video

* Create a caption

* Explain how you would distribute the content

* Provide 3 additional content ideas based on the footage





**We are looking for someone exceptional who wants to grow with PB Agency long-term.**

title: Recruitment, People & Compliance Administrator – UK Care Home Group

Draft letters,
s and basic employment documents

Strong organisational skills

title: Operations & Marketing Virtual Assistant
description:

This is not primarily a customer service or social media role.



We are looking for someone who enjoys systems, organisation, data, processes and getting things done accurately.



You will work closely with the CEO and our operations team to help make the business more organised, automated and efficient.

 campaigns from approved copy/templates

 graphics and campaign materials

* Are extremely organised and detail-oriented

How to Apply

We are looking for someone who wants a stable, long-term working relationship and who can grow in responsibility as trust and experience develop.

title: Instagram DM Marketing Expert For Collabs (Lead Gen & Outreach)
description:
Job Title: Instagram Cold DM Marketing Expert for Creator Collaborations (Hourly + $50/Collab Bonus)



About the Role



We're looking for an experienced Instagram DM marketer who knows how to start conversations that convert without torching the account in the process. Your goal is simple: reach out to content creators, build genuine conversations, and land content collaborations for our brand. You'll own our Instagram outreach channel end to end, covering strategy, execution, tracking, and reporting. That includes creating, warming up, and bringing to life the new Instagram accounts that will be used for the cold DMs. This is a hands-on role, and you run it yourself.



What You'll Do



• Create the new Instagram accounts that will be used for cold DM outreach, including profile setup, branding, and positioning so they look like real, active accounts from day one

• Warm up each account properly before any outreach begins: aging, gradual activity increases, and normal engagement patterns

• Post content and bring the accounts to life: feed posts, stories, and reels, plus genuine day-to-day engagement so they stay healthy, active, and credible

• Plan and execute Instagram cold DM outreach campaigns to content creators that generate qualified conversations and booked collaborations

• Build and maintain a prospect list of 20,000 to 30,000 target creator accounts based on criteria we provide (niche, follower range, engagement quality)

• Manage day-to-day engagement: outbound DMs, replies, follow-ups, and story-based nurture. You're the first point of contact creators see, so you represent the brand

• Track reply rates, conversation rates, and collaborations closed, then iterate weekly

• Write and A/B test DM scripts and collab pitches that feel human and personal, not copy-paste spam

• Report results directly to the owner



Requirements (Must-Haves)



• Proven experience managing Instagram cold DM outreach campaigns, with results you can show

• Hands-on experience creating and warming up Instagram accounts for outreach, and keeping them alive with regular posting and engagement so they stay in good standing

• Experience pitching collaborations, partnerships, or ambassador deals to creators is a big plus

• Deep understanding of Instagram's rate limits, automation policies, and what actually keeps accounts in good standing (we want sustainable growth, not account churn)

• Ability to run campaigns independently, start to finish, including account creation, warm-up, and content posting

• Strong written English and conversational instincts, since creator outreach lives or dies on tone

• Familiarity with outreach/CRM tracking (spreadsheet or tool of your choice)

• Be willing to work in controversial niches**



Compensation



• $4.60 USD/hour

• $50 USD bonus per successfully executed collaboration with a content creator (target: 6 completed collabs/month once scaled)

• Part Time (May evolve into full time if we can scale to 50 Instagram accounts to dm people) If we're getting results, we'll ramp it up more and you can take on more responsibility like scheduling and logistics. If you want more work I can always find more for you to do.



How to Apply



Reply to this job post with "IG cold DM genius" in the subject line. Applications without it will not be reviewed.



In your reply, include an answer to only 1 of the following:



• Your experience with Instagram cold DM campaigns: niches, volume, and results (reply rates, leads generated, collaborations or sales closed)

• Your experience creating and warming up Instagram accounts, and how you keep them active and healthy long term

• Any experience specifically pitching creators for collabs, sponsorships, or partnerships

• The tools you've used (automation, scheduling, tracking, CRM)

• How you structure outreach so accounts stay healthy and compliant long-term

• A short example DM opener you'd use to pitch a content collaboration in our niche



You'll be evaluated on your demonstrated ability to manage Instagram DM campaigns and your past results, not generic marketing claims.

Every day, you will receive raw video clips from our shop floor (printing presses running, orders being made, finished products) and talking-head recordings from the owner. Your job is to edit these into short-form and long-form videos optimized for each platform.



This is a high-volume role. You will produce 8–15 edited video pieces per day across different formats. Speed, consistency, and understanding of what makes content perform on social media are essential.



What you will do

Short-form video editing (primary focus — 70% of time)

• Edit raw clips into 15–60 second videos for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts

• Add captions/subtitles to all videos (burned-in, styled, readable)

• Write and add text hooks in the first 1–2 seconds of every video

• Add transitions, zoom effects, and pacing that match platform trends

• Select and sync trending audio/music where appropriate

• Create satisfying loop videos from production process footage (press pulls, ink shots, transfer peels)

• Edit before/after reveal videos with dramatic transitions

• Format and resize the same video for different platforms (9:16, 1:1, 16:9)



Long-form video editing (20% of time)

• Edit 1 long-form YouTube video per week (5–15 minutes)

• Full process walkthroughs: a single order from design to shipping

• Educational content: print method comparisons, branding guides, industry tips

• Add intro/outro, lower thirds, chapter markers, and b-roll where needed

• Create compelling thumbnails for YouTube videos



Ad creative (10% of time)

• Edit short video ads for Meta 
/Instagram) campaigns

• Create multiple variations of the same ad for A/B testing

• Follow direct creative briefs from the Content Manager



Daily output expectations

• 8–10 short-form videos (TikTok/Reels/Shorts format) per day

• 2–3 Stories-format clips per day

• 1 long-form YouTube video per week

• 1–2 ad creatives per week

III. Final Interview

title: Real Estate VA: Property Onboarding, Purchasing & Reconciliation
description:
REAL ESTATE VIRTUAL ASSISTANT: PROPERTY ONBOARDING, PURCHASING AND RECONCILIATION



Please read this whole post before applying. There are instructions at the bottom, and how you follow them is the first thing we look at.



ABOUT US



We run full-service, hands-off management for short-term rental owners across the US. An owner hands us an empty house. We furnish it, wire it, stock it, style it, photograph it, license it, connect it to the booking channels and open it to guests. Then our management team runs it.



That middle part is a project with about two hundred moving pieces and a hard finish line, and right now it lives almost entirely in our founder's head. That is the whole reason this seat exists. Most days are a spreadsheet, a vendor invoice, a receipt, a permit portal and a follow-up list.



We automate everything software can do. What software cannot do is notice that a vendor invoice and a card statement disagree by $16.48 and go find out why, or notice on day one that the internet install is booked eleven days out and the permit needs a floor plan that nobody has drawn yet.



We are growing. Our written plan is 150 managed doors by the end of 2027. This is the first seat of its kind here and it will not be the last one.



WHAT THIS ROLE REALLY IS



Two lanes, one person. Every case below is real. Money amounts are changed, for a reason we explain further down. The shapes are all real.



LANE ONE, THE RECORD OF THE MONEY.



Nineteen furniture lines on a live property are flagged as ordered. There is no order number behind any of them, no charge on any card, and no confirmation from the vendor. Either they were bought and nobody wrote it down, or somebody typed a word into the wrong cell. The difference is $4,318.62. If you place that order and it was already placed, the owner pays for the same furniture twice, and nobody finds out for a month.



- Two lines carry the same item name and two different product links, so the house is getting either four sofas or two, a $2,144.75 question, and the owner is reading it as one line.

- A vendor invoice hit the card as $9,340.55 on the 12th and another $812.07 on the 19th, because that vendor captures payment as items ship. The record held only the first number, so the property looked $812.07 cheaper than it was.

- A tax column on an Oregon delivery showed $22.50 per mattress and nothing on the other sixty items. That is not tax. It is a state recycling fee that is legitimately owed, and two people here have already gotten it wrong.

- A four-figure order shipped to one property's address and belonged to a different property's plan. The ship-to address is never the answer. The item list is.

- One plan column read $10,462.31 against an order total of $10,462.08. A twenty-three cent gap between two numbers computed from completely different inputs made the row look reconciled while the real figure underneath it sat $1,384.90 low.



LANE TWO, GETTING THE HOUSE TO THE FINISH LINE.



A house is furnished, wired, cleaned and photographed, and it still cannot take a guest, because the city permit needs a floor plan, the floor plan needs a measured scan nobody has ordered, and the internet install is booked eleven days out. Somebody has to know that on day one, not in week five.



- Four separate deliveries land at a vacant house in one week. Three arrive, one is refused at the curb for freight damage, and the replacement ships to the wrong state. A box left at the door of an empty house is nobody's until somebody is named, and you are the person who names them.

- A utility account is open, but it is in the previous owner's name, autopay is off, and we are not listed as an authorized contact, which means the day the power goes out nobody at that utility will speak to us.

- A city changes its short-term rental rules mid-project. The registration the property was counting on no longer exists and the path is now a discretionary hearing. Finding that out in week two is a plan change. Finding it out in week nine is a dead launch.

- The listing goes up with the nightly rate still on the platform's starter default, the maximum stay set to 365 nights, and the house rules field empty. Every one of those is a field somebody had to set, and nobody did.

- Eight vendors are needed before the first guest: cleaner, plumber, electrician, HVAC, handyman, landscaper, pool, pest. Sourcing them is the easy half. The hard half is that every one of those phone numbers has to be dialed once before we call it a directory.



The honest description of this role: it is detective work on money, and chasing on everything else. It is quiet and it is deliberate.



The person who is great at it is the person who genuinely cannot leave a number alone when it does not tie, who would rather spend forty minutes finding the missing $16.48 than type over the cell and move on, and who also will not let a utility company, a permit office or a busy designer go three days without an answer.



This is not task-list work. Nobody is going to send you a list each morning telling you which rows to price or which office to call. You run a weekly rhythm and a countdown you can read yourself, so you already know.



If that reads as tedious to you, we would genuinely rather you skip this one. If it reads as a puzzle with a deadline, keep going.



WHAT YOU WILL OWN



THE BUDGET RECORD. One Google Sheet per property, our launch budget tracker. It is the single record of what the property is buying, what it committed to, what actually got charged and what is left. Every property in flight has one and you run all of them.



- Price every row on the plan that has no price. Find the item, confirm the variant, the size and the pack quantity, and put a real number on it.

- Load the purchasing carts against the plan. This has real traps. Our cart holds a hard 50 lines, and line 51 silently pushes the oldest line out into Saved for later, so a 152 row accessories list is four separate orders and you d
 the batches up front. Re-adding an item that is already in the cart raises its quantity instead of warning you. You verify by item code and quantity, never by the badge in the corner.

- Tag every order back onto the plan rows it paid for, so nothing is bought that the sheet does not know about.

- Log every card charge as its own row, with the invoice's true order total rather than the first posting that showed up, and file the receipt the day it exists. A charge with no receipt cannot be cleanly billed back, which means a missing receipt is money the company cannot recover that month.

- Reconcile every vendor invoice against what we actually committed to, line by line, and produce the defect list. What was charged, what was ordered, what is missing, what does not agree, and which of those is a real problem versus a coi
.

- Run the flag pass every Friday. Filter the exception column and clear everything that is not clean. Some of our checks run from scripts on our side and we run them against your sheet, so your pass has to be clean before it reaches them.

- Chase our designer for the receipts, the property attributions and the open answers that nobody else is going to chase. The buying happens in person, in other states, on a company card, and store receipts print department codes instead of product names, so only the person who was standing there can say which room a $340 receipt belongs to.

- Open a tracker for a new property from our template and type the house into the quantity calculator: bedrooms, beds by size, baths, sleeps, TVs, floors. Half the quantities calculate themselves off those numbers, so this is not data entry, it is the foundation. Every count comes from a written source, and when two written sources disagree you flag it instead of picking a winner.

- Watch the envelope. The plan has a cap, and the week you first see that the plan is going to cross it, you say so out loud. Weeks early, not at the end.

- Produce the close-out: the reconciliation that says whether the owner is owed a refund or owes a true-up, and the drafted invoice or refund figure behind it.



THE COUNTDOWN. From the day the management agreement is executed to the day our management team can run the house without you.



- The calendar itself. Every property on one board, every gate current, every date real. You own the answer to "where is this house and what is it waiting on," and you own it before anybody has to ask.

- Accounts and utilities. Every account to Active in the correct name, us named as an authorized contact with call-in and outage rights, autopay and paperless set, and the internet ordered with the install date captured the day it books. That date is the longest lead time in most launches.

- Licensing, permits and tax. Research the market's short-term rental rules and confirm the property qualifies before anyone spends money assuming it does. Assemble the permit application, including the floor plan. Open the portal account, submit, and track it to ISSUED. Send the neighbor notices where they are required. Get the permit number into every advertisement. Register the lodging and occupancy tax accounts and record which channel remits what.

- Insurance and the vendor bench. Chase the certificate of insurance and file it. Source and qualify the local vendor bench, capture after-hours rates, and get recurring landscaping, pool and pest started so the first visit lands before the first guest.

- The physical fate of every order. The delivery calendar, tracking numbers, backorders, what arrived, what did not, what arrived damaged, what got reshipped and when, what got returned.

- Listing provisioning. Import the property into our management system and map every field. Confirm the two-way calendar and rate sync. Connect our pricing tool. Connect our cleaning tool, assign the cleaner and apply the right checklist. Expand to the additional channels. Stage all of it and hand it to us to publish.

- The property record. The project folder, the property file, the contact list, the service directory, warranty registrations off the serial numbers collected during install, the placement map, opening inventory counts, and the archive when it closes.

- Owner logistics, and only logistics. Signature status, a utility account number, a certificate of insurance, an app invitation that has not been accepted. Chased under our name, never yours, and never carrying a number.

- The measurement. Days from signature to first booked night, per property, recorded. Nobody here has ever written that number down. You will be the first.



HELPING BUILD THE SYSTEM. We have a written playbook for this seat and we are still finishing the SOPs behind it. You will help write them, in your own words, out of the work you actually did. As we add properties this becomes more than one seat, and the person who runs it well is the person who trains the next one.



WHAT YOU WILL NOT DO, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT SECTION IN THIS POST



Two walls. Both are deliberate, both are permanent, and neither bends for a deadline.



THE MONEY WALL: YOU OWN THE RECORD, YOU NEVER OWN THE MOVEMENT.



Nothing you do debits a bank, releases a wire, pays a card, or reaches an owner's inbox. Not once, not in an emergency, not on a deadline.



- You never fire a charge. Every single payment, card or eCheck or wire, is approved personally by our founder, on that specific charge, every time. There is no batch approval and there is no standing permission.

- You never move money out of any bank or merchant account. You compute what should be paid and you evidence it. He releases it.

- You do not place the orders. You build the cart, you verify it line by line, you hand it over with the batch, the total, the shipping address and the property reference it needs, and somebody else presses the button.

- You are not the property owner's contact. Not the approval schedule, not an invoice, not a refund figure, not an
 with a number in it. You draft. We send. Always.

- You never add, edit or verify a vendor's bank details or payee information. Nobody in this seat does. That is the wall against invoice fraud, and urgency is the exact pretext it exists to defeat.

- You have no banking, no payment gateway and no accounting system access, on purpose. If you ever find that you somehow can reach one, you do not act, you report it.



THE BUILDING WALL: YOU RUN THE COUNTDOWN, YOU NEVER CERTIFY THE HOUSE.



You are remote. You will never stand in these houses. So there is a category of work that is structurally not yours, and we would rather you know that now than discover it in month two and feel set up to fail.



- You never certify a physical condition and you never sign a walkthrough. You schedule it, you receive its findings, you turn them into dispatched work and you track them to done. You do not perform it and you do not sign your name to it.

- You never name anyone, including yourself, as a city's required local contact. That is a legal representation about a person who can physically reach a property, and it is our founder's to make.

- You never publish a listing. You stage it completely, every field set. He calls go or no-go.

- A house being ready is not your call to make. You produce the evidence that it is. Somebody standing in it makes the call.



Read both walls as protection, not as distrust. The seat that keeps the record of the money is deliberately not the seat that moves it, because a record that can move money is not a record, it is an opinion. The seat that runs the countdown is deliberately not the seat that certifies the building, because a countdown that can declare itself finished is not a countdown. Those separations are what make your close-out number and your green light worth something, and they mean that when money or a guest goes somewhere it should not have, it is structurally impossible for it to have been you. We designed it that way on purpose, we will not ask you to bend it, and we think it is one of the best parts of the offer.



A WORD ABOUT CONFIDENTIALITY



You will see what we pay for goods and what the owner is billed for them. That information does not leave the company, ever, for any reason, including to an owner who asks you directly and including when they are being nice about it. If that is not a line you can hold comfortably, please do not apply. It is written into the agreement and we take it seriously.



The same applies in the other direction. You never structure anything: no splitting an order, sequencing a purchase, or shaping a number so it sits under a threshold. And no order, vendor or reimbursement that benefits you or anyone connected to you. Either one is immediate cause, even if the underlying purchase was perfectly fine.



MUST-HAVES



We are not going to write "detail oriented" here, because everybody says it about themselves and it predicts nothing. Here is what actually predicts success in this seat.



- 2+ years in a role where reconciling one document against another was the actual job. Accounts payable, bookkeeping, procurement, e-commerce operations, inventory control, order desk, audit support. Something where a number had to tie and you were the one who made it tie.

- You know that a total matching is not proof it is right. Two numbers built from completely different inputs can land within a dollar of each other by coi
, look tied, and hide a four-figure error underneath. Somebody who checks totals and stops will not survive here.

- You understand that one number can arrive as several charges. A single vendor order can hit a card as three postings weeks apart. Log the first one and the record is quietly wrong forever, and nothing on the sheet will tell you.

- You chase small discrepancies to the bottom. If a total is off by $16.48, we need the person who finds the $16.48, not the person who adjusts the total.

- You can hold an open discrepancy without doing either wrong thing with it. The two failure modes are dropping it because it is small and inventing a reason for it because you want it closed. Both are worse than a note that says "unexplained, $16.48, chasing." If you have ever kept a variance open for two weeks because you refused to guess, tell us about it.

- You have run something with a deadline and many moving parts, and you can show us the instrument you ran it on. A launch, an onboarding, a move, an event, an implementation, a store opening. Not "I am organized." The actual tracker, board or sheet, and what you did the week it started slipping.

- You follow up politely and repeatedly with somebody who is busy, who is not your subordinate, and who has no reason to prioritize you. Utility companies, city permit offices, vendors, a designer in another state. This does not resolve itself and it is a large part of the job's value.

- You leave alone what you do not understand. Some of our sheets carry hand-marked rows whose meaning was never written down. Our standing rule is preserve, never interpret. A near-pattern is a trap, not a shortcut, and finishing one makes six edits nobody can undo.

- Real spreadsheet fluency, not "proficient in Excel" on a resume. SUMIFS, lookups, filters, spotting a hardcoded number sitting where a formula should be, and knowing what happens to a sheet when someone inserts a column into the middle of it. We will test this and it is not a hard test if this is true of you. You do not need to code.

- You can tell someone senior to you that a number is wrong, or that a date is not going to hold. Comfortably, in writing, with the evidence attached. Bad news early is the single most valuable thing you will ever send us.

- Stamina for a long pass. Some days are 150 rows of the same check. We need the 150th to get the same attention as the first.

- Honest. If you have not confirmed something, you say so. You never report a status you did not verify and you never invent a number, a price, a quantity, a receipt, a confirmation or which property a charge belongs to. "I do not know yet, here is how I am finding out" is always the right answer. This is the single most important item on this list and it is a hard gate at every stage of our process.

- Clear, professional written English. You will write to US vendors, US city offices and a US designer about money and deadlines.

- Stable power and internet, plus a backup for outages.

- Able to work the fixed shift below. Please read the hours section carefully before you apply.



NICE-TO-HAVES



- Property management, real estate operations, or short-term rental background.

- You have dealt with a government or municipal office and got a thing issued. Permits, licensing, registrations, business filings, customs, anything where a form met a bureaucracy and you won.

- Trade, wholesale or B2B purchasing account experience.

- You have reconciled a credit card statement against a set of vendor invoices and found something.

- You have chased a vendor for a credit and won.

- Bookkeeping exposure, QuickBooks or Xero or similar, even read-only.

- Furniture, interior design, hospitality FF&E, or construction procurement background.

- Experience with a property management system, a dynamic pricing tool, or a cleaning scheduling tool.

- You have built a tracker or a process that somebody else then used without you in the room.

- A little Google Apps Script or Python, or genuine curiosity about the scripts behind our sheets. Not required. Rewarded.



HOURS AND TIMEZONE



This is a fixed US business-hours shift. Please read the conversion below carefully.



- The shift is 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM US Pacific, Monday through Friday. Eight hours a day, forty hours a week. You are online and responsive for the whole of it.

- In the Philippines that is 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM, starting the following day. It is an overnight shift. Pacific is fifteen hours behind Manila in US daylight time, so an 8:00 AM Pacific start is 11:00 PM in Manila and a 4:00 PM Pacific finish is 7:00 AM in Manila. We are stating that plainly so nobody works out the math after they have accepted.

- The shift moves by one hour in Manila terms when the US changes to and from daylight saving time. The Pacific hours stay 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

- Why this window and not a later one. Half this job is other people's business hours. Utility companies, city permit offices, vendor support and freight carriers on the US East Coast close at 2:00 PM Pacific. This shift gives you six hours of overlap with them. A later shift would give you three, and you would spend your life waiting a day for every answer.

- Some deadlines in this job are actual dates. The Friday flag pass happens on Friday. Ordering deadlines and permit windows are the other kind, and they do not move.

- No weekends. No overnight emergencies outside your shift. Those stay with us.



Be honest with yourself about the overnight window before you apply. If 11:00 PM to 7:00 AM does not fit your life, please do not apply, and there is no hard feeling in that.



If you are somewhere other than the Philippines, do the conversion yourself and tell us on the form what 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM Pacific is where you are. We do read that answer.



COMPENSATION



- $1,000 per month, for the arrangement above.

- The rate is flat. It does not step up as the scope grows. We would rather say that plainly than describe an increase we have not committed to, so you can plan on this number.

- Merit review at 90 days after conversion, then annually. That is where the rate gets revisited.

- We honor 13th month pay. We offer flexible coordinated time off and we cover your equipment. We treat our people well and the good ones grow with us.

- Paid trial first. Before any ongoing offer there is a short paid project, a couple of hours of real work, and we pay you for it.

- The first four weeks are an Initial Evaluation Term at close to full rate, so both sides get a real look before anyone commits.



HOW WE HIRE



We use a multi-step process and it is deliberately demanding. Every stage is something you do on your own time, and we do not schedule a single call until you have already shown us how you work. In order: a short application form, a 2-minute video, a written reconciliation exercise, a personality assessment, then an interview and a paid trial. Budget roughly two to three hours of your own time across all of it before the paid trial, which we pay for. The personality assessment is a tiebreaker, not a gate, and nobody is rejected on it alone.



The reconciliation exercise is the stage that d
 this seat. It is a real invoice against a real plan with the names taken out, it does not tie, and the reason it does not tie is not the reason you will first think it is. There is no trick, but there is a wrong answer that most people give, and it is the confident one.



We move fast, and you set the pace. There is no application window and no waiting for a batch. Each stage unlocks the moment you finish the one before it, and every deadline is measured from when the
 reaches you, not from a date on our calendar. Somebody who moves promptly can go from applying to a paid trial in a couple of weeks.



Deadlines are real at every stage. If you miss one, you are out. Please do not ask for an extension.



HOW TO APPLY



Fill out the form linked at the very bottom of this post.



Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed. Please do not message us on this platform, do not
 us, and do not send a resume in a reply. Only form submissions are looked at. We know that is strict. It is the first filter and it is working as intended.



Read the form carefully. One of the questions is there to check that you read this post.

If you're the kind of person who double-checks a form before hitting submit, you'll fit right in.

• Handle real volume multiple videos a day, across multiple channels without dropping quality or missing a slot

• Fast, reliable internet you can count on daily the single most important requirement for this role

• Full-time availability, every day we publish this is a high-volume role and needs someone with the time to give it consistently

• Meticulous with detail a wrong tag or a mistimed publish is exactly what this role exists to prevent

• Decent written English for titles and descriptions

• Experience uploading to or managing more than one YouTube channel
