title: CRO Specialist – Deep Audit of 200+ Session Replays (Shopify Store, Ad-to-Purchase Journey)
description:
Hi! I run a DTC e-commerce brand on Shopify and most of our traffic comes from paid ads (Meta). I'm recording hundreds of session replays on our store (over 200 so far) and I need someone to watch them properly and tell me exactly where and why visitors get lost after clicking an ad.



This is an important role. I am NOT looking for someone who runs everything through AI and sends back a generic checklist. I'm looking for a person who actually watches the sessions, takes notes, spots patterns and backs every recommendation with real evidence.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Watch and analyze 200+ session replays recorded with Microsoft Clarity and Propel

- Map the real customer journey: ad click > landing page > product page > cart > checkout

- Check if the site keeps the promise of our ads (same message, same offer, same visual feel). I will share our current ads and a description of our typical customer

- Identify friction points: confusion, rage clicks, dead clicks, drop-offs, hesitation, missing information, trust issues, mobile problems

- Tell us what to change: copy, layout, flow, and where better graphics or visuals are needed



WHAT YOU WILL DELIVER

A written audit (Google Doc or similar) with:

1. The top issues, ranked by expected impact on conversions

2. For each issue: replay links + timestamps showing it, how often it happens, why it matters

3. A concrete recommendation for each issue (what to change and where)

4. A short section on ad-to-site consistency: where the site breaks the expectations created by the ads

5. Quick wins vs bigger changes, with a rough effort estimate



REQUIREMENTS

- Proven experience with CRO / UX audits on e-commerce (Shopify is a plus)

- Real experience analyzing session recordings and heatmaps (Microsoft Clarity, Hotjar or similar)

- Understanding of paid traffic and how ad messaging affects landing page behavior

- Strong written English and the ability to explain WHY, not just WHAT

- Patience and attention to detail: this job is about watching carefully, not about speed



HOW WE WORK

- Project-based, with the possibility of ongoing work if the audit is good

- Shortlisted candidates will first do a PAID TEST: analyze 10 replays and send us their top 3 findings



MANDATORY SELECTION TEST - APPLICATIONS WITHOUT THIS WILL BE IGNORED



To prove you read the whole post, START YOUR SUBJECT LINE WITH "REPLAY AUDIT -" followed by your name. Applications without it will not be opened.



Then answer these 4 questions IN YOUR OWN WORDS (AI-generated answers are easy to spot and will be rejected):



1. Describe ONE real finding you discovered by watching session recordings for a past client or project. What was the problem, what did you recommend, and what changed after?

2. A visitor arrives on a product page from a
 ad on mobile, scrolls a little, stops for 8 seconds, then leaves. What would you look at in that replay to understand why, and what could the possible causes be?

3. How would you organize the analysis of 200+ replays so you don't miss patterns? Be specific (tagging, segments, filters, notes).

4. Have you used Microsoft Clarity before? Which other tools have you used for session replays and heatmaps?



Please also include:

- 1-2 examples of audits or CRO reports you have done (links or screenshots, confidential data can be hidden)

- Your availability and how many days you need for the full audit

- Your rate for the full project



Thank you, I look forward to finding the right person!

title: Office Manager / Dispatcher / Inside Sales - ServiceTitan - US HVAC (Cleveland, Ohio)
description:

READ THIS WHOLE POST BEFORE APPLYING. Applications that skip the three requirements at the

bottom are deleted without a reply. We are not being rude - we have hired before and we are

done wasting time.



WHO WE ARE

Raber HVAC - heating, cooling, plumbing and electrical in Cleveland, Ohio. Real company,

real technicians in the field every day, growing fast. We run everything on ServiceTitan.



WHO WE WANT

One person to run our office. You are the voice of this company on the phone. When a customer

in Cleveland has no heat at 7am, you are who they talk to. You d
 which technician goes

where, you keep the board full, and you turn phone calls into booked jobs.



This is not a "virtual assistant" job and it is not a data-entry job. This is the person who

holds the office together and pushes revenue up. If you do that well, you will be paid like

someone who does that well - there is a monthly commission on top of your base, uncapped.

The better this company does, the more you make. We want somebody who wants that.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Answer every inbound call and convert it into a booked job. We measure your BOOKING RATE.

- Run the ServiceTitan dispatch board: assign and move technicians, optimize the day, handle

  same-day and emergency calls, keep the board tight.

- Follow up on unsold estimates until they close. This is real money and it is your money too.

- Sell and renew memberships.

- Outbound calls: recall lists, aging estimates, past customers.

- Keep job notes, customer records and scheduling clean in ServiceTitan.

- Coordinate with the technicians all day - by phone and by text.



HOURS

Monday to Saturday, 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM Cleveland time (US Eastern). 60 hours a week.

That is 8:00 PM to 6:00 AM Manila time. This is a NIGHT SHIFT for you. Be honest with

yourself before you apply - we need you sharp at 3am your time, every night, for years.



PAY

1,600 to 1,800 US dollars a month base, depending on what you actually bring, PLUS an

uncapped monthly commission on what the office produces. A strong person here clears

2,500 to 3,000 a month. There is no ceiling on the commission - that is the whole point.

Tell us the monthly number you need. Serious, experienced people are paid seriously here.



=====================================================================

THE THREE REQUIREMENTS - NO EXCEPTIONS

=====================================================================



1. ENGLISH - SPOKEN, FAST, CLEAR, NEUTRAL ACCENT

   You will be on the phone with American homeowners all day. They must never have to ask you

   to repeat yourself. If you have worked US voice accounts in a call center and Americans

   understood you easily, that is what we are looking for.



   *** SEND A VOICE RECORDING WITH YOUR APPLICATION. 60 TO 90 SECONDS. ***

   Do not send a script you read out loud. Answer this, out loud, as if it were a real call:



     "A homeowner calls at 7:00 AM. Her furnace is dead, it is 20 degrees outside, she has a

      baby in the house and she is upset. Our first open slot is Thursday. What do you say to

      her, word for word, and what do you do in ServiceTitan?"



   No recording = no reply. This is the first thing we listen to.



2. EXPERIENCE - WE DO NOT TRAIN

   You must already know ServiceTitan and you must already know US home services

   (HVAC / plumbing / electrical). Day one you run the board on your own.

   In your application, name the US company you did this for and for how long, and say exactly

   what you did in ServiceTitan: dispatch board, scheduling, invoicing, unsold estimates,

   memberships, pricebook. "I am a fast learner" is not an answer to this.



3. INTERNET AND POWER - PROVE IT

   Our last hire went dark mid-shift because his line was cut and he had no backup. Never again.

   Send us:

   - a speedtest.net screenshot from where you will actually work

   - proof of a BACKUP INTERNET connection (mobile hotspot / second provider)

   - proof of BACKUP POWER (UPS or battery that keeps your router and computer alive)

   - one sentence: what do you do the moment the power dies at 2am in the middle of a shift?



   We do not accept excuses about internet or power. Ever. If that sounds harsh, this job is

   not for you.



=====================================================================



HOW TO APPLY

Reply with: (1) your voice recording, (2) your ServiceTitan / US home-services history with

company names and dates, (3) your internet and power proof, (4) the monthly number you need

and for how many hours a week, (5) your WhatsApp number.



Anything missing and we move on to the next person. Everything included and you will hear

from us within 24 hours.

title: Video Editor
description:
**READ THIS FIRST — DO NOT APPLY WITHOUT THESE**



We are looking for a full-time editor with a proven track record editing long-form lifestyle YouTube videos in the travel/van life/adventure space.



Your editing style should match the quality and feel of channels like Trent the Traveler. If you are not familiar with Trent the Traveler's videos, go watch several of his videos on YouTube before applying. That is the editing style, pacing, and storytelling quality we expect.



You must be fluent in English. You will be editing dialogue-driven storytelling content, so you need to understand every word being said in order to nail the pacing, cuts, and emotional beats.



If you do not have experience editing this style of content or are not fluent in spoken and written English, please do not apply.



ABOUT US:

We are full-time content creators with over 800,000 subscribers and followers across multiple platforms (YouTube, Instagram,
, X/Twitter, TikTok). Our primary YouTube channel produces long-form lifestyle travel and van life content (20–45 minutes per video). We need an editor who understands this genre inside and out — the pacing, the storytelling, the emotional beats, and the way these videos hold viewers from the first second to the last.



WHAT YOU'LL DO:

You'll work with both edited and raw footage to produce finished videos that are engaging, professional, and tell a compelling story. This includes long-form YouTube videos (20–45 min) and short-form content (Shorts, Reels, TikTok under 60 sec).



You must be proficient in trimming, cutting, and arranging footage into cohesive narratives; adding transitions, music, sound effects, and visual effects; color correction and grading; text overlays, captions, and graphics; pacing and structure for both long-form and short-form content; and adapting editing style to match platform requirements (YouTube, Instagram, TikTok).



We need someone who is fast, reliable, has a natural storytelling instinct, and is passionate about creating content that pulls viewers in from the first second and keeps them watching.



TO APPLY — ALL OF THE FOLLOWING ARE REQUIRED (incomplete applications will not be reviewed):



1. Your email address.

2. The video editing software you use and the type of computer you edit on.

3. Your expected hourly rate.

4. CLICKABLE LINKS to exactly 3 long-form lifestyle/travel YouTube videos you have edited. These must be published videos on YouTube that we can watch right now. They should demonstrate your ability to edit in the style described above — think Trent the Traveler level pacing, storytelling, and production quality. If your portfolio does not reflect this style and level of editing, please do not apply.

5. Clickable links to 2 short-form video projects you have edited (Shorts, Reels, or TikTok).

6. Visit 
 and perform an internet speed test. Post your results for both upload speed and download speed.



COMPENSATION:

$5 – $8 per hour depending on experience, ~40 hours per week.



SKILLS REQUIRED:

Fluent in English (spoken and written), Long-form video editing (20–45 min YouTube videos), short-form video editing (Shorts, Reels, TikTok), high attention to detail, strong storytelling ability, creativity, and fast turnaround.

title: Long-Form YouTube Video Editor – Travel & Lifestyle
description:

We are established travel and lifestyle content creators with nearly 1 million combined subscribers and followers across multiple platforms. We are hiring a full-time long-form YouTube editor for our creator-led travel, RV, van-life, outdoor, and adventure channel.



Our finished videos are generally 20–45 minutes long. We need an experienced editor who can turn several hours of raw footage into a compelling, story-driven YouTube video—not simply arrange clips in chronological order.



This position is focused on long-form YouTube content, not Shorts, Reels, podcasts, gaming videos, or corporate content.



ABOUT THE EDITING STYLE



A strong style reference for this position is Trent the Traveler.



Before applying, watch several of his long-form YouTube videos and become familiar with his storytelling, pacing, dialogue editing, music selection, sound design, scenic sequences, humor, and emotional timing.



We need an editor who can:



• Find the strongest story within several hours of raw footage

• Create compelling openings that immediately build curiosity

• Structure each video with a clear beginning, middle, and end

• Edit natural conversations without making them feel rushed

• Remove repetitive, unnecessary, or weak footage

• Use music, sound effects, B-roll, and scenic footage effectively

• Build anticipation and maintain viewer interest

• Know when an edit should move quickly and when a 
nt should breathe

• Turn everyday travel experiences into entertaining long-form stories



ENGLISH FLUENCY IS REQUIRED



You must be highly fluent in spoken and written English.



Our videos include natural conversations, humor, sarcasm, reactions, emotional 
nts, and storylines that develop throughout the footage. You must understand the dialogue, tone, and context well enough to make strong decisions about pacing, cuts, music, and emotional timing.



THE ROLE



You will edit complete 20–45 minute YouTube videos from raw footage through final delivery.



You must be able to:



• Review several hours of raw footage and identify the strongest story

• Create a compelling opening and clear beginning, middle, and end

• Edit natural dialogue while preserving humor, emotion, and pacing

• Remove repetitive, unnecessary, or weak footage

• Use music, sound design, B-roll, scenic footage, and travel montages effectively

• Clean and mix audio and perform basic color correction

• Add text, maps, captions, and graphics when needed

• Follow editing notes, complete revisions accurately, and apply feedback consistently

• Meet deadlines, work independently, and communicate clearly

You must have proven experience editing long-form, creator-led travel, lifestyle, RV, van-life, outdoor, or adventure YouTube videos.



You must also have strong storytelling instincts, excellent attention to detail, reliable high-speed internet, a dependable editing computer, and availability for approximately 40 hours per week.



HOW TO APPLY

I READ THE LONG-FORM VIDEO LINK REQUIREMENTS

1. YOUR INFORMATION



• Full name

• Email address

• Current city and country

• Editing software and computer you use

• Expected hourly rate

• Weekly availability

• Normal working hours in Philippine Time

• Earliest available start date

• Whether you currently have another full-time job or major ongoing clients



2. YOUR TOP THREE LONG-FORM VIDEO EDITS



Provide EXACTLY THREE direct, clickable links to individual, published YouTube videos that you personally edited.



All three videos must:



• Be at least 15 minutes long

• Be creator-led travel, lifestyle, RV, van-life, outdoor, or adventure videos

• Link directly to the actual published video

• Clearly demonstrate your long-form storytelling and editing ability



At least one must be a travel, RV, or van-life vlog with storytelling, pacing, and production quality similar to Trent the Traveler’s long-form videos.



For each video, include:



• The direct YouTube link

• The channel name

DO NOT SEND:

• Demo reels

• YouTube channel homepages

• Playlists

We will only review the three direct video links you submit.



Applications without exactly three qualifying direct video links will not be reviewed.



3. RELEVANT EXPERIENCE



In one short paragraph, describe your experience editing long-form travel, lifestyle, RV, van-life, outdoor, or adventure YouTube videos.

In one short paragraph, explain how you turn several hours of raw travel footage into one compelling 20–45 minute YouTube story.

Provide your Speedtest.net results:



• Download speed

Include a screenshot or public result link.

?

?



Engagement structure

?

 1. What systems have you enforced rules or workflows in?

 3. Are you comfortable working inside unfamiliar systems without step-by-step instructions? (Yes/No)



No long cover letters needed.



?



Important



This role exists to make systems behave correctly — not to explain why they should.



If that sounds obvious to you, you’re likely a fit.

title: Systems Enforcement Engineer (Billing / RevOps / Internal Systems)
description:
Overview (read this carefully before applying)





We are looking for someone who has already implemented hard rules inside live business systems, rules that prevent processes from continuing until a required condition is met.







This is not a research role.



This is not a “figure it out” role.



This is not a consulting or advisory role.







If your background is primarily:



website development



feature building



general automation



experimentation



“I can build something for this”







This is not a fit.







We only want people who already do this kind of work in production environments.



The Type of Work





You will be responsible for configuring system-level controls inside real companies so that:



Certain business actions cannot proceed



Until a specific required action is completed



With clear ownership, logging, and escalation







Examples of the kind of enforcement we mean:



Revenue cannot be billed until required data exists



Deals cannot close until approvals are recorded



Billing cannot proceed unless contract terms are present



Access cannot be granted without verification



Workflows halt until required steps are completed







If you have personally implemented rules like this before, you will immediately recognize the work.



What You Must Already Have Done





You should apply only if you can confidently say yes to all of the following:



You have implemented hard workflow rules in live systems



You have blocked or gated business processes on purpose



You have worked inside billing, payments, CRM, RevOps, ERP, or internal tools



You understand how to enforce rules without breaking production systems



You have dealt with stakeholder pushback when enforcement was introduced







If you’ve never stopped a business process from continuing until a condition was met, this role will not work for you.



What You Will Not Be Asked To Do

You will not design strategy



You will not “explore options”



You will not experiment



You will not pitch ideas



You will not build customer-facing features







Your job is execution only.







You will be given:



A clearly defined condition that must be enforced



A bounded scope



A finite timeline







Your responsibility is to make the system obey the rule.



Typical Systems Involved (varies by client)





You may work inside environments that include:



Billing & payments systems



CRMs



Revenue operations stacks



Internal databases



Workflow automation tools



Access control systems







Exact tools vary. The logic does not.



Engagement Structure

One-time, fixed-scope implementations



Clear start and end conditions



No ongoing retainers



No open-ended support







If you prefer long-term consulting relationships, this is not a fit.



How to Apply (Required)

1.





Describe a real example where you implemented a system rule that prevented a business process from continuing until a required condition was met.



What was blocked, where was it enforced, and why?







2.





What type of company was this implemented in (size, business type), and what systems were involved?







3.





What changed operationally once the rule was enforced?







If you cannot answer these from real experience, do not apply.



Final Note





This role is for people who are comfortable enforcing constraints, not just building tools.







If that sentence resonates immediately, you’re likely a fit.



If it doesn’t, you won’t enjoy this work.

title: Systems Control Installer (Operations / Automation)
description:
We are looking for a competent systems operator who can enter unfamiliar business environments and make specific operational conditions true.







This is not a role for someone who needs step-by-step instructions.







You will be given a clear, written specification of what must be true inside a company’s systems. Your job is to translate that specification into reality using the tools and systems already in place.







Think of this like a field technician role, but for internal business systems instead of physical hardware.



What You Will Do

Enter existing business systems (CRM, billing, product, ops tools, etc.)



Review a short reference document describing a required control or constraint



Identify where the control must live inside the system



Configure workflows, permissions, automations, or blocks so the condition becomes true



Request access or clarification only when necessary



Deliver a clean, working result — not documentation, not explanations







You are not designing strategy.



You are not consulting.



You are making something impossible to ignore or bypass.



What This Role Is 

Not

Not data entry



Not virtual assistance



Not customer support



Not a call-heavy role



Not a role with constant supervision



Not a role with detailed instructions







If you need someone to tell you how to do things, this is not a fit.



Required Traits (More Important Than Tools)

Comfortable entering unknown systems and figuring them out



Strong internal sense of accountability (“if it breaks, I fix it”)



Able to translate written requirements into system behavior



Calm under ambiguity



Zero ego — focused on outcome, not credit



Can work independently once access is granted







If you’ve ever worked as:



a field technician



a systems admin



an automation specialist



an internal ops implementer



a “fixer” who gets dropped into messy setups







You’ll understand this role immediately.



Technical Experience (Flexible)





You do not need to know every tool.







Experience with some of the following is helpful:



CRMs (Salesforce, HubSpot, etc.)



Automation tools (Zapier, Make, native workflows)



Billing systems



Permissions / role-based access



Internal tooling or admin panels







What matters more is that you can learn fast and execute cleanly.



How Work Happens

Work begins after client payment



You receive a clear reference document



You request access



You implement



You confirm completion



You move on







No meetings unless absolutely required.



Compensation

Paid per engagement or per install



Rates discussed after initial screening



Reliable, ongoing work for the right operator



How to Apply (Important)





In your application, do not send a generic cover letter.







Instead, answer briefly:



Have you ever entered a system you didn’t know and figured it out anyway? (Yes / No)



Do you prefer clear outcomes over detailed instructions? (Yes / No)



Describe one situation where you were dropped into something unfamiliar and made it work. (3–5 sentences max)







Applications that do not answer these will be ignored.

Collect and organize all relevant evidence

title: Instagram Content Clipper, Editor & Poster — 2 Coaching Business Pages (Daily)
description:
We run a personal branding / coaching business (Done4U), and we're hiring ONE reliable, experienced content VA to run TWO business Instagram accounts: 



1) Our official Done4U business page — a page built on PROOF: testimonials, client wins, and our best coaching moments.

2) A second content account for our business partner Jake 
 — a higher-volume educational page: clipped YouTube, raw "yaps," and talking-head reels. 



Both pages represent our brand. Everything posted has to look sharp, consistent, and on-brand — every single post. This is a strict, high-standard role with clear SOPs for both accounts. Read carefully. If you skim job posts, miss details, or need hand-holding on every cut, this is not for you.



WHO THIS IS FOR:

This is a taste-driven, experience-required role. You must already know how to clip long-form content down into short-form — pulling the perfect 30–60 seconds out of a 90-minute call or a full-length YouTube video. You should instantly recognise a hook, a moment, and a payoff worth posting. You must also be a genuinely capable editor.



WHAT YOU'LL DO (daily, across both accounts):

- Go through our raw footage (
 / Google Drive) and pull the strongest moments.

- Clip and edit cleanly in CapCut: trim tight, add clear captions, crop to vertical 9:16 (and 16:9 where briefed), and keep a consistent premium look.

- Done4U page: log in and post 2–3 clips per day, mixing content types, following the SOP.

- Jake's 2nd account: produce a steady volume of clips across three styles — (A) YouTube clipped up, (B) raw yaps, (C) talking-head reels — matching locked brand fonts, colours, and caption styles, and post/schedule when approved.

- Keep simple trackers updated so nothing is ever posted twice.



THE CONTENT YOU'LL BE CLIPPING:

- Mastermind sessions, 1:1 coaching calls, and community coaching calls

- Full YouTube videos from two accounts — clipping the best moments from across the whole video, not just the intros

- Talking-head / piece-to-camera footage and raw "yaps"

- Occasionally a coach's content (in the form of community calls and YT moments)



NON-NEGOTIABLES — you MUST:

- Have real, proven experience clipping long-form footage into short-form (SEND EXAMPLES TO BE CONSIDERED).

- Be a strong editor in CapCut — captions, trimming, text, basic keyframes/zoom, vertical + landscape export.

- Have genuine taste — you know what's worth posting and what isn't.

- Be comfortable logging into Instagram and posting 2–3 times a day, every day, following an SOP exactly.

- Follow written brand locks precisely — fonts, colours, caption styles, safe zones. No inventing your own look.

- Be proactive and self-sufficient — use the SOPs, figure things out, and only ask when it genuinely matters. We do not have time for a hundred questions a day.

- Treat the brand as sacred — image, structure, and consistency come first, always. Every post must look like it belongs to the same premium page.

- Be reliable, detail-oriented, and consistent. This is a daily role and misses get noticed.

- Have a laptop/phone that can edit and export 1080×1920 and 1920×1080 without crashing, plus stable internet. Comfortable with 
, Instagram, and Google Sheets.



TIMEZONE: We often work to Asia/Dubai (UTC+4). State your timezone and daily working window.



WHAT YOU GET:

- $3 USD/hour, with raises based on performance.

- Full SOPs and clear direction for both accounts — you'll know exactly what to look for.

- A steady, long-term role for the right person.



Honest note: $3/hr is an entry rate and we're upfront about it (there is potential for raises with performance - we are looking for long term team members)

title: U.S. Bookkeeping & Accounting Professional
description:
Immediate Opening



We are looking for a full-time accounting professional in the Philippines who wants to build a long-term career working with U.S.-based clients.



This position is a little different from a typical bookkeeping role, so please read the entire description before applying.



What the Role Looks Like



For the first 1 to 3 months, a significant part of this position will involve high-volume data entry for one U.S. client.



This client processes a large number of transactions, potentially 50 to 100+ invoices per day, across both accounts payable and accounts receivable. You need to be comfortable working accurately and efficiently with this level of volume.



We want to be very clear about this upfront. If you dislike repetitive, high-volume transaction entry, this probably isn't the right position for you.



However, the position will not stay this way.



We are actively working to automate much of this process. Sales and AR activity will eventually flow from ServiceTitan into the accounting system, and AP invoices will increasingly be processed using OCR and automation tools.



As those systems are implemented, your role will shift from primarily entering transactions to reviewing transactions, monitoring automated processes, bookkeeping, reconciliations, and working with additional U.S. clients.



Our expectation is that this position will eventually support approximately 3 to 5 U.S. clients, starting with our less complicated accounts. As your skills and knowledge grow, there will be opportunities to take on more complex accounting responsibilities.



What We're Looking For



We would especially like to hear from candidates who have:



* Experience working directly with U.S.-based clients, preferably multiple clients

* Strong experience with QuickBooks Online

* Experience with bookkeeping, bank reconciliations, AP and AR

* Experience processing a high volume of invoices or other financial transactions

* Strong attention to detail and accuracy

* The ability to work efficiently with repetitive tasks without sacrificing quality

* Good written and verbal English communication skills

* A reliable, high-speed internet connection and dependable home work environment

* An interest in learning new accounting systems and technology

* A genuine interest in working with and eventually supporting multiple U.S. businesses



Experience with ServiceTitan would be a major plus, but it is not required.



Work Schedule



This is a full-time, 8-hour-per-day position working U.S. hours.



Your regular workday will end at 2:00 AM Pacific Time, so please make sure you are comfortable working this schedule on a long-term basis before applying.



We strongly prefer candidates who have previously worked a night or graveyard schedule for U.S. clients and already know that this schedule works for them.



Where This Position Can Go



We're not looking for someone just to enter invoices.



We're looking for someone who can handle the high-volume work required at the beginning, learn our clients and systems, and then grow into a broader accounting and bookkeeping role.



As we automate the repetitive work, we want to give you more responsibility and expose you to additional U.S. clients. For someone who wants to develop their U.S. accounting experience, there is significant room to grow.



How to Apply



Please submit both of the following:



1. Your resume

2. A short video introduction, approximately 1 minute



In your video, please briefly tell us:



* Your accounting/bookkeeping background

* How much experience you have working with U.S. clients

title: Operations Manager
description:
# Operations Manager — Customer Experience & Dispatch



Remote · Full-time · Fixed monthly compensation of $2,000–$3,000 · Minimum 40 hours per week, with additional availability for urgent operational needs



## About Dropcurb



Dropcurb coordinates curbside junk removal and partner donation pickups through independent haulers. We are hiring an experienced operations manager to lead our dispatch team, protect the customer experience, and build reliable processes as we grow.



You will work directly with the founder and own how daily operations perform. You should be comfortable handling a difficult order yourself, teaching someone else how to handle it, and improving the process so the same preventable problem becomes less likely to happen again.



## Commitment and availability



This role requires a minimum of 40 hours per week and flexibility to provide additional support when urgent operational issues need attention. We will agree core working hours, aligned with Dropcurb's operating needs, and escalation coverage before you start.



When a serious issue needs management support, step in, coordinate the right people, and follow it through to a verified resolution. Maintain dependable coverage and accepted handoffs. Retain responsibility for urgent issues until a capable owner accepts them or they are resolved, and improve the process to reduce preventable emergencies.



## What you will own



**Learn and run the operation.** Learn our dispatch workflow, customer journey, service boundaries, quoting approach, and tools. Investigate knowledge gaps and become capable of sound independent decisions within agreed limits.



**Exercise pricing judgment and oversee agent use.** Dispatchers handle routine quotes and hauler payouts with our quoting agent. You handle exceptions, spot-check quality, and train the team. Verify scope, access, capacity, timing, comparable jobs, and costs. Check that the agent received sufficient context and produced a sensible answer. Apply established prices and approval limits.



**Make the daily basics dependable.** Establish and verify coverage for inbound calls, prompt messages, required Craigslist posts, shared
, daily review responses, and publishing founder-prepared social posts. Keep work owned through interruptions, absences, and handoffs.



**Protect the customer experience.** Review open and completed orders for broken promises, excessive waiting, customer chasing, inappropriate late pickups, unexpected changes, and poor recovery. Act when commitments become at risk and investigate bad experiences before a complaint or review.



**Respond to urgent issues.** Recognize refund requests, frustrated customers, hauler problems, payment discrepancies, and safety concerns. Take appropriate immediate action, communicate clearly, and verify resolution. Maintain escalation and handoff coverage beyond your core shift.



**Improve processes at the cause.** Investigate why work is lost or mistakes recur. Establish practical routines, checks, ownership, and escalation. Verify adoption and results. Implement useful fixes with existing tools and make evidence-backed requests for software improvements.



**Build and manage a strong team.** Define performance standards, interview through realistic work scenarios, and verify claimed expertise. Run focused team reviews, teach the reasoning behind decisions, check understanding with a new example, and inspect subsequent work. Coach gaps and make evidence-based staffing recommendations.



**Hire and manage a GBP specialist.** Learn the Google Business Profile workflow sufficiently to scope the work and qualify a proven expert for verification, profile health, optimization, and suspension/support issues. Start with the actual workload, verified expertise, and clear deliverables.



**Use AI effectively.** Apply AI to suitable analysis, service review, coaching, and documentation. Verify conclusions against source records and policy, correct errors, and assess whether the workflow improves speed or quality.



## Experience and abilities we are looking for



- Proven hands-on management of a small team responsible for completing time-sensitive service work. Relevant backgrounds include dispatch, home services, field service, transportation, delivery, and comparable operations.

- Specific examples of processes you personally improved, how you got staff to adopt them, and how you verified the result.

- Strong customer-experience judgment, including recognizing when a completed job still represents a poor experience.

- Practical commercial judgment, clear reasoning with incomplete information, and appropriate escalation.

- An established method for managing commitments, notifications, priorities, and follow-through.

- Experience assessing, training, and managing staff, with clear evidence of your personal responsibility.

- Clear spoken and written English for customer, hauler, and team communication.

- Ability to validate the quoting agent's output and train staff to supply sufficient context. Broader experience using AI for analysis and process improvement is a strong advantage.



Experience building processes in a startup or small growing business is preferred. We value initiative, speed, hands-on ownership, and improvements that continue working across shifts. Previous use of our exact CRM is not required. GBP specialist experience is valuable; the manager must be able to assess and manage the expert doing that work.



## How success will be assessed



We will agree priorities, access, authority, service standards, and a baseline during onboarding. Success means dependable daily coverage, fewer preventable misses, earlier detection of customer and hauler problems, sound quoting decisions, adopted process improvements, and less avoidable founder intervention. Material issues must remain visible and receive appropriate escalation.



## How to apply



Send your resume and brief answers to the following:



1. Describe one recurring operational failure you personally reduced. What was the cause, what did you change, and how did you verify the improvement?

2. Describe a customer-experience problem you caught without waiting for a complaint. What did you do, and what happened?

3. What team and workload did you directly manage? What decisions could you make independently?

4. Describe one AI-assisted workflow you actually use, the result it improves, and how you check its output.



Use specific examples and identify your personal contribution. Anonymize confidential information; approximate figures are acceptable when labeled.



Shortlisted applicants will complete a paid practical assessment using fictional operating records. It includes prioritization, customer recovery, process design, quoting, hiring judgment, and AI use. Finalists may proceed to reference checks with consent and a paid supervised trial or structured onboarding period, with terms and expectations agreed in advance.

title: AI VIDEO EDITOR — FULL-TIME REMOTE | UP TO $3,000/MONTH

description:
We’re hiring an experienced Google Business Profile specialist to own profile creation, verification, optimization, and ongoing management across our local markets. You’ll also work directly with interested people, guiding them through the setup and verification process and following through until each next step is completed.



You must have direct, hands-on experience creating and verifying profiles, managing multiple listings, and handling suspensions and reinstatement appeals. We need someone who can bring their expertise, identify problems, and move work forward independently.



You will be responsible for:

- Profile creation and verification: Assess location eligibility, set up accurate profiles, configure categories, services, hours, contact information, and booking links, and manage verification through completion.



- Hauler outreach and coordination: Contact interested haulers, explain the process clearly, collect necessary information, schedule walkthroughs, and guide them through verification requirements, including video verification when required.



- Suspensions and reinstatements: Investigate the issue, identify and correct underlying problems, gather legitimate supporting documentation, submit appeals, and manage follow-ups with Google.



- Ongoing optimization: Keep profiles complete and accurate, improve relevant categories and services, maintain photos and posts, and identify opportunities to improve local visibility and customer conversion.



- Review management: Monitor and respond to reviews in a professional, natural voice. Flag customer concerns to the appropriate team and follow through on unresolved issues.



- Profile monitoring: Check for verification problems, unexpected edits, duplicate listings, inaccurate information, and other issues that could affect visibility or customer trust.



- Performance reporting: Track profile visibility, website clicks, calls, and attributable bookings where tracking is available. Explain what changed, what you believe caused it, and what action you recommend.



- Organization and follow-through: Maintain a clear tracker for every profile and hauler, including current status, open issues, last contact, next action, and follow-up date.



To be considered, you must have:

- Personally created and verified Google Business Profiles, including service-area businesses and location-based businesses.

- Direct experience handling suspensions and reinstatement appeals, with examples of your work and outcomes.

- Experience managing multiple profiles at the same time.

- A working understanding of Google’s current business representation guidelines and suspension appeal process.

- Strong written and spoken English, with the confidence to guide haulers over calls, messages

- The ability to troubleshoot independently, recognize when an issue needs escalation, and follow up without repeated reminders.

Experience with U.S. home services, local SEO, citation audits, and managing profiles across multiple markets is a plus.

Success in this role means accurate, verified profiles; haulers who understand and complete their next steps; timely review responses; well-managed suspension cases; and measurable progress toward qualified inquiries and bookings.

title: Short-Form Video Editor & Creative (Ads + Social) - Sports/Fitness DTC Brand
description:
We're a fast-growing sports & fitness DTC brand. We make water-filled instability training gear used by athletes, coaches, and everyday people who want to move and feel better. Our growth runs on video - short-form ads and organic social - and creative is the single biggest lever we have. You'd join a small, fast team and own a big part of what the world sees.



THE ROLE

You turn raw footage, UGC, and briefs into scroll-stopping short-form video for Meta, TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts - both paid ads and organic posts. Formats: UGC, hooks, problem/solution, testimonial, product-focus, VSL-style, and fresh angle/hook variations of what's already winning. Roughly 1 in 4 videos will use AI generation to extend or reimagine winning angles.



THIS IS NOT THE ROLE IF...

...you log on and wait to be told every cut, send three "just checking?" messages, and need every concept handed to you. It's also not weddings, corporate, or long-form YouTube.



THIS IS THE ROLE IF...

- You understand the algorithm and viewer psychology - why people stop, watch, and buy - and can say WHY an edit works, not just make it look nice.

- You bring your own concepts: you watch what's hitting on our socials and competitors', and pitch new ideas and hooks without being asked.

- You take ownership - you read the brief once, look at our last few winning videos, and ship something that belongs next to them, right the first time more often than not.

- You're resourceful: you find footage, music, and solutions yourself instead of getting stuck.

- Strong on pacing, captions, sound design, and light motion graphics.



NICE TO HAVE

- AI video tools (Higgsfield, Kling, Veo, Runway, ElevenLabs) - a real plus, about 25% of our work.

- Track record on performance / direct-response ads for a DTC / ecommerce brand.

- Sports, fitness, rehab, or anatomy / movement content experience.



HOW WE WORK

No micromanaging - do great work and you get freedom and a clear path to grow into a creative lead / strategist. Base salary + uncapped performance bonuses tied to what your videos deliver. Full-time, remote, long-term, with some daily overlap with EU (Amsterdam) hours.



HOW TO APPLY (READ CAREFULLY)

Apply here: 
 - the short form takes about 5 minutes. It asks for:

1. An explainer video (MOST IMPORTANT): a short clip of YOU - on camera or voiceover - walking through one of your own edits: what you did and WHY. We hire on how you think and communicate, not just how you cut.

2. Two or three of your best short-form ads or social videos (links).

3. A brand you admire on social - why their videos work (hook, psychology, retention).

4. One video concept you'd make for a water-filled training product, and the hook you'd open with.

5. The monthly pay you're looking for (your asking rate) and the AI tools you use.



Make every video link viewable - if it's a Google Drive link, set sharing to "Anyone with the link", or we can't open it.



Shortlisted candidates get a small paid test edit before we hire. We review every application through the form above, so please apply there rather than only messaging here.

title: Business Development Associate
description:
What you own



You generate new business from zero. No inbound lead, no existing relationship, no warm intro required — you find who should be working with us, reach them by call, email, or DM, and pitch them on it. You own the entire arc from first contact to signed engagement.



This is not chasing something already agreed to. That's a different seat. You're creating the "yes" in the first place, with people who don't know we exist yet and have no reason to reply to you.



Once something's signed, it's handed off to get built and delivered. Your job ends at the close, not before it, and not indefinitely after it — you're not managing the relationship forever, you're the reason it started.



What disqualifies you

-A generic pitch that doesn't change based on who you're actually talking to

-Overpromising to close — misrepresenting what we actually do isn't a sales technique here, it's a liability we'll have to clean up

-Going quiet after a rejection instead of adjusting and trying the next one

-Needing leads handed to you. If you're waiting to be given someone to call, that's not this role

-Losing track of what's actually been said to whom — sloppy pipeline tracking creates problems for everyone downstream of you



What you need

-A real track record of generating net-new business through outbound — cold calls, cold email, cold DMs, not warm referrals dressed up as cold outreach

-Genuine comfort with rejection and repetition, without needing each attempt to land to keep going

-Sharp enough listening to actually customize a pitch in real time, not just recite one

-No specific degree or credential required



How we hire for this



Not a narrative interview. Talking about how you'd handle a cold call and actually running one are two different skills, so we test the second one directly.



Application: a few standard questions on how you approach outreach, rejection, and follow-up. Not scored as truth — it's the baseline we check your live performance against.



Live round: you'll actually pitch — a real (simulated) cold call or cold outreach scenario, run live. You'll get real objections, real pushback, and direct correction on your approach at least twice in the same session. We're not scoring a polished first pitch. 

We're scoring whether your second attempt is sharper than your first, and whether you can take a note on your approach without getting defensive about it.



If you can start something from nothing and make it land, apply.

title: Operations Program Manager / Chief of Staff
description:
Engineering Studio 



What you own



You're handed a defined goal — already scoped, already d
. From there it's yours: build the plan, identify who needs to move, get them moving, track whether it's actually happening, escalate the 
nt it stalls. You're accountable for outcomes on programs that don't belong to any single team.



You also keep the operating rhythm of the studio intact. That means running the meeting cadence, following up on the commitments people actually made, and making sure decisions get implemented — not just discussed and quietly dropped. When a decision gets made, you make sure everyone affected understands what it means for them, specifically, and actually does it. Catching agreement that wasn't real internalization — before it turns into silent non-alignment — is core to this job, not a side task.



You'll have real, appropriate authority in your scope. Not proximity dressed up as influence, not soft power you have to negotiate for every time. Real authority, held accountable.



You are not shaping strategy — that stays upstream. You are the reason strategy turns into something real, and the reason nothing falls through the cracks between the decisions made and the people executing them.



What disqualifies you



Needing to be managed, reminded, or chased. We manage work, not people.

Explaining intent when corrected instead of fixing. If the correction was clear, "why" isn't needed — only the adjustment.

Agreeing in the room, then not actually internalizing or executing the decision.



What you need



A track record of owning outcomes across teams that don't report to you

Real systems thinking — you see how the pieces connect, not just the next checklist item

Comfortable being the one who says the uncomfortable, accurate thing when a decision isn't actually landing

The ability to take a live correction and produce a clean fix, fast, without it becoming a conversation about you

No specific degree or credential required.



How we hire for this



Not a narrative interview. We've found what people say about handling correction and what they actually do under real, live correction are two different tests — so we run the second one.



Application: a few standard questions about how you approach structure, correction, ambiguity. Not scored as truth. It's a baseline we compare against what we see live.



Live round: real (anonymized) program material, worked through in real time, with direct correction delivered at least twice in the same session. We're not scoring whether your first answer is right. We're watching the gap between the correction landing and the fix starting — and whether that gap shrinks the second time.



If you can take a clear correction and move without needing it softened, apply.

What the job is



We sell supplements on a subscription. We are good at acquiring customers. We are not good at keeping them, and we know it: a large share of our subscribers write in to cancel before their second charge, and we are losing money we already paid to acquire.



That is this job. You own retention. Not the tickets — the numbers behind them. You d
 what we say when someone wants to leave, what we offer, when we offer it, and what we change upstream so they stop wanting to leave in the first place.



We are hiring for judgment, not for tasks. You have done this at a subscription brand before and you know what works because you watched it work.



Your work



1. Find out why they leave, with evidence. Read the cancellation reasons, the support inbox, the refund requests, the chargebacks. Group them. Tell us the three real reasons people churn, ranked by how much money each one costs us. Not opinions — counts.



2. Build the cancellation flow. What we ask, in what order, what we offer against each reason. Pause, skip, change frequency, downsize the order, one-time discount, product swap. You d
 the ladder and where the discount sits in it, because a discount given too early is margin we never get back.



3. Fix the money we lose silently. Failed payments and dunning. Card updates. Retry logic. Most subscription brands lose more subscribers to a declined card than to an actual decision to quit, and nobody notices because nobody complains.



4. Work the first 60 days. The subscriber who cancels before charge two never got the product to work. Onboarding emails, dosage expectations, what to feel and when, proactive check-ins. You write the plan and brief whoever executes it.



5. Win them back. Cancelled subscribers are the cheapest customers we will ever have. Build the sequence that brings a share of them back.



6. Report what you changed and what it did. Churn by cohort, retention curve by month, LTV, save rate on cancellation requests, recovered failed payments. Monthly, in numbers, with what you will do next.



What we need from you



You have run retention for a subscription DTC brand. Not "I did support at a brand that had subscriptions" — you owned the churn number and you were judged on it.



You know the tools properly: Recharge, Skio, Bold, Loop or similar, and the email side (Klaviyo or equivalent). You have configured them, not just used them.



You can read a cohort. If we hand you six months of subscriber data, you can tell us where the drop happens and what it is worth.



You have opinions about save offers, and you can defend them. When to pause instead of discount. When a refund is cheaper than a chargeback. When to let someone go.



You write clearly. The emails and flows you design are read by customers, so the words matter.



You have seen this before at another brand. We are not the first place where you learn this.



Nice to have



Supplements, health or wellness specifically. Experience setting up a support function from scratch — helpdesk, macros, refund policy, SOPs. Managing or training support agents. Chargeback dispute experience.

Some of our brands are in health and women's wellness, including intimacy products. The work is never explicit, but if that topic is not for you, this role is not for you and that is completely fine.

 the offers and the flows. No committee.

Right now nobody owns that chain. Orders get placed when someone remembers. Stock counts live in different places and do not always agree. We find out we are running low when support starts getting emails.

6. Report weekly. Stock position, incoming shipments and dates, cash tied up in inventory, anything at risk in the next 30 days. Short, in numbers.

You have done inventory or supply chain for an e-commerce brand, not just warehouse admin. You have placed real purchase orders with real money behind them.

title: Meta Media Buyer - Restricted E-Commerce
description:
READ THIS FULLY BEFORE APPLYING. There are specific application instructions at the bottom. Applications that ignore them are deleted unread. This is deliberate, and it is the first test.



ABOUT US



We're a North American based performance marketing agency. We run Meta advertising for e-commerce brands in restricted and regulated categories: canna and CBD accessories, nicotine, spirits, and research peptides. These are underserved brands in acute pain, and we get them live and spending fast.



We are small, direct, and we do not micromanage. What we need is people who close their own loops.



WHAT THIS ROLE ACTUALLY IS



This is not a role where you inherit warm accounts and tune creative. Roughly half this job is keeping ad accounts alive, and the other half is getting campaigns live before they die. If that sounds unappealing, stop reading. You will be unhappy here.



Day to day: sourcing and warming profiles, BMs and ad accounts; billing and verification; building and publishing campaigns across multiple accounts and brands; appeals and reinstatement; and reporting status in writing without being asked.



YOU MUST HAVE



- Hands-on Meta buying experience in restricted, grey or high-risk verticals. Mainstream dropshipping or local lead gen alone is not enough.

- YOUR OWN ACCOUNT SUPPLY CHAIN, or a clear and specific process for building one. This is the single most important requirement. If your answer is "I use whatever the client gives me," you are not a fit.

- Real experience with appeals, business verification, and what actually gets accounts reinstated versus what wastes a week.

- Pixel and Conversions API setup, BM structure, and enough technical comfort to debug tracking yourself.

- Written English strong enough to explain a problem clearly the first time.



HOURS



Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM to 3:00 PM Philippine time. Fixed.



We deliberately do not want anyone working past midnight their own time. Outside those hours you are off, with one narrow exception for a disabled account or runaway spend.



PAY



7 to 10 USD per hour depending on demonstrated experience, paid twice monthly. Starts with a paid two-week trial on one client, at full rate. Performance review at 60 days.



HOW TO APPLY



Send a message with the subject line: APEX - [Your Name] - Account Supply



In the body, answer these five. Short and specific beats long and polished:



1. Where does your ad account, BM and profile supply come from? Describe the actual process, not the outcome.

2. It is the morning after a ban wave and four accounts are down. What are your first three actions, in order?

3. Send Ad Library links to accounts you are running right now.

4. What is the longest you have kept an account alive in a restricted vertical, and what finally killed it?

5. Tell us about a time you had to tell a client something would not be done on time. What did you say?



Do not send a generic portfolio.

title: Dispute Manager – Shopify & PayPal
description:
# Job Opening: Dispute Manager – Shopify & PayPal



**Position:** Dispute Manager & Supply Chain Coordinator

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

**Salary:** $3 per hour

**Work Arrangement:** Remote



## About the Role



We are looking for an experienced Dispute Manager with a strong background in Shopify and PayPal dispute resolution, chargeback management, and ecommerce operations. The ideal candidate should be capable of handling payment disputes, minimizing financial losses, and maintaining accurate transaction records.



In addition to dispute management, this role will involve working closely with our supply chain operations, including monitoring incoming and outgoing products, reviewing supplier quotations, verifying pricing, and coordinating order fulfillment.



## Key Responsibilities



### 1. Dispute & Chargeback Management



* Handle Shopify Payments disputes, PayPal disputes, chargebacks, and payment-related customer complaints.

* Prepare and submit compelling evidence and documentation within the required deadlines.

* Monitor dispute cases, track outcomes, and maintain detailed records.

* Investigate fraudulent transactions, unauthorized payments, and item-not-received claims.

* Identify recurring dispute patterns and recommend ways to reduce chargebacks and financial losses.

* Coordinate with customer support and fulfillment teams to resolve disputes effectively.



### 2. Supply Chain Management



* Monitor products coming into and going out of the business.

* Review supplier quotations, invoices, and product costs to verify pricing accuracy.

* Compare supplier prices and identify discrepancies or potential cost-saving opportunities.

* Track order fulfillment, shipping updates, delivery delays, and missing or damaged products.

* Coordinate with suppliers and logistics partners to resolve operational issues.

* Maintain accurate records of inventory movements, supplier transactions, and order statuses.



### 3. Reporting & Operations



* Prepare regular reports on dispute rates, chargeback outcomes, and financial exposure.

* Maintain organized documentation for disputes, suppliers, and order-related issues.

* Work alongside the management team to improve payment operations and supply chain efficiency.



## Required Qualifications & Experience



* **Proven professional experience** managing disputes and chargebacks for Shopify and PayPal.

* Practical experience preparing and submitting dispute evidence through Shopify and PayPal platforms.

* Strong understanding of ecommerce payment processes, refunds, chargebacks, and fraud-related claims.

* Previous experience in supply chain management, supplier coordination, order fulfillment, or inventory operations.

* Experience reviewing supplier quotations, invoices, and product pricing.

* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

* Good written and verbal communication skills.

* Ability to work independently, meet deadlines, and manage multiple responsibilities.



## Preferred Qualifications



* Experience working with Shopify stores that process a high volume of orders.

* Familiarity with payment dispute prevention tools and ecommerce fraud indicators.

* Experience using spreadsheets, inventory management systems, and order tracking tools.

* Ability to prepare clear operational reports and identify process improvements.



## Compensation



**Base salary: $3 per hour.**



Performance-based salary reviews and potential increases may be considered based on demonstrated results, reliability, and overall contribution to the business.



## How to Apply



Please submit your application with the following information:



1. Your relevant experience managing Shopify and PayPal disputes.

2. Examples of dispute and chargeback cases you have handled.

3. Your experience with supply chain management and supplier coordination.

4. The tools and platforms you have previously used.

5. Your availability and expected working hours.



**Important:** Applicants must have practical, hands-on experience in both dispute management and supply chain operations. We are looking for someone who can take ownership of these responsibilities and contribute to the smooth operation of our ecommerce business.
